SOMMAIRE
Des précédents favorables à Feyenoord à domicile
Trois points chacun après quatre journées, un seul succès de part et d’autre. Feyenoord et le FC Porto se retrouvent mardi 24 novembre à Rotterdam dans une situation délicate en Ligue des champions. Les deux clubs, engagés dans la course aux places qualificatives pour la phase à élimination directe, ont besoin de se relancer lors de cette cinquième journée. Le coup d’envoi est fixé à 21 heures, heure de Cotonou.
Leurs dernières sorties européennes ont pourtant été très différentes. Porto a battu Naples 4-1 le 4 novembre après trois défaites consécutives dans cette phase de ligue. Feyenoord, lui, s’est incliné 3-0 à domicile contre l’Inter Milan la veille. La formation néerlandaise a désormais perdu dix de ses treize derniers matches européens, selon les données de l’UEFA publiées vendredi 20 novembre.
Les difficultés de Feyenoord apparaissent particulièrement au début des rencontres. Le club a encaissé le premier but lors de ses sept derniers matches de Ligue des champions, sa plus longue série dans l’épreuve. Une statistique qui donne du poids à l’entame du match contre Porto, même si les résultats passés ne préjugent pas du scénario de mardi.
Des précédents favorables à Feyenoord à domicile
Le stade De Kuip a néanmoins souvent réussi aux Rotterdamois face aux équipes portugaises. En sept réceptions européennes de clubs du Portugal, ils comptent trois victoires, trois nuls et une seule défaite. Porto, de son côté, n’a remporté aucun de ses quatre derniers déplacements chez des adversaires néerlandais, avec deux nuls et deux revers.
Les deux formations se connaissent. En Ligue Europa 2019-2020, Feyenoord avait gagné 2-0 à Rotterdam avant de perdre 3-2 à Porto. L’histoire des effectifs crée d’autres liens. Gonçalo Borges a quitté les Dragons pour Feyenoord en juillet 2025, alors qu’Inbeom Hwang a effectué le trajet inverse l’été dernier. L’Algérien Anis Hadj Moussa, auteur d’un but lors du  succès de Feyenoord contre Côme (3-2)  le 14 octobre, figure parmi les joueurs offensifs du club néerlandais.
Porto a retrouvé de l’efficacité devant le but lors de sa  victoire contre Naples . Feyenoord doit, lui, renouer avec le résultat qui avait lancé sa campagne. La rencontre au De Kuip opposera ainsi deux équipes à égalité au classement, mais dont les dernières trajectoires européennes divergent.

La gendarmerie sénégalaise a interpellé cinq suspects dans une enquête sur des vols de téléphones suivis d’opérations d’hameçonnage. La chanteuse Aïda Samb figure parmi les victimes recensées.

La Section de recherches de la gendarmerie de Colobane a interpellé cinq suspects le 14 novembre dans une enquête sur un réseau de téléphones volés au Sénégal. La chanteuse Aïda Samb figure parmi les victimes recensées dans ce dossier.
Son iPhone lui avait été dérobé le 23 septembre. Selon les éléments d’enquête rapportés par Seneweb, le vol a été suivi d’une opération d’hameçonnage qui aurait permis de retirer 1 002 000 francs CFA de son compte Wave.
Le procédé consistait à envoyer aux propriétaires de faux liens imitant le service « Localiser » d’Apple. Les identifiants iCloud saisis sur ces pages étaient ensuite utilisés pour déverrouiller les appareils avant leur revente ou leur acheminement hors du pays.
Les perquisitions ont permis de saisir 19 iPhone, un iPad, un ordinateur, 29 cartes SIM, trois dispositifs de type Turbo SIM et deux motocyclettes. Les enquêteurs ont également exploité les numéros IMEI et les données téléphoniques recueillies après plusieurs plaintes pour des vols suivis d’accès frauduleux à des comptes Wave ou Orange Money.
Le dossier comprend aussi le vol de deux téléphones survenu le 31 octobre pendant l’ouverture des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse à Dakar. L’ambassadeur d’Arabie saoudite au Sénégal et Halima Guèye comptent parmi les victimes mentionnées.
Les gendarmes poursuivent leurs recherches pour identifier d’autres membres présumés du circuit, soupçonné d’avoir acheminé des appareils vers la Gambie et le Maroc. Les cinq personnes arrêtées doivent être présentées au parquet de Pikine-Guédiawaye au terme de l’enquête.

items.title: IGAD Media Awards Emerge as One of Africa’s Best Platforms for Journalists: Workneh

original_payload.original_title: IGAD Media Awards Emerge as One of Africa’s Best Platforms for Journalists: Workneh
original_payload.original_body:
Addis Ababa, November 21, 2026 ENA)— The Intergovernmental Authority on Development IGAD Executive Secretary Dr. Workneh Gebeyehu has described the IGAD Media Awards as one of Africa’s leading media recognition platforms.
The Executive Secretary emphasized media professionals’  growing contribution in the region to bringing regional journalists together, amplifying credible African voices, and reshaping narratives about the Greater Horn of Africa.
The IGAD Media Awards 2026 recognized around 20 journalists last night from member states, celebrating outstanding journalists and storytellers whose work is shaping public conversations and transforming narratives across the Greater Horn of Africa.
Speaking to ENA, Dr. Workneh said the initiative had grown significantly since its launch in Djibouti four years ago, reflecting its expanding regional reach and impact.
“When we started this initiative four years ago in Djibouti, it was not like this. It was not as big as it is today. Without fear of contradiction, I can say that this is one of the best media awards in Africa,” he said.
He highlighted two major achievements of the awards: fostering regional connections among journalists and recognizing the contributions of African media professionals in telling the continent’s own stories.
“First, the goal is to bring regional journalists together, bringing credible voices from across the region onto one platform to share experiences. Second, it is about appreciating our own journalists. Our stories should be told by our own sons and daughters,” he emphasized.
Dr. Workneh said the initiative was moving in the right direction, particularly in strengthening regional media cooperation and promoting African perspectives on issues affecting the region.
Turning to IGAD’s broader mandate, he stressed that the persistent challenges facing the  Horn of Africa, including peace and security threats, climate change, drought, and food insecurity; require collective regional responses rather than isolated national efforts.
Established in 1986, IGAD was founded to address shared regional challenges, and its role in coordinating member states' efforts remains essential, he noted.
“These challenges are not confined to one country, and no single country can win the battle against the challenges facing this region,” he said.
He underscored the importance of IGAD as a regional platform for pooling efforts, mobilizing resources, exchanging experiences, and sharing successful practices among member states.
While acknowledging the resilience demonstrated by the region, he stressed that stronger commitment from member states remains essential to overcoming the challenges.
Although the region has yet to overcome all its difficulties, collective action remains the most effective way forward, he added.

original_payload.original_title: FinHealth: Public Financial Management in Health Diagnostic Toolkit 2.0
original_payload.original_body:
Why do some health facilities run short of medical supplies, or leave posts for health workers unfilled? Part of the answer can lie in how public money for health is managed.
FinHealth: Public Financial Management in Health Diagnostic Toolkit 2.0, a joint product of the World Bank and the World Health Organization (WHO), helps countries find these underlying causes and resolve them. It starts by asking what is not working for health systems and seeks to identify the underlying public financial management bottlenecks that contribute to these shortcomings.
The Toolkit guides teams through four steps. They identify and prioritize the health service problems to focus on, map the organizations, funding flows and public financial management rules involved, identify the bottlenecks behind each problem and their root causes, and develop concrete, actionable recommendations.
This updated Toolkit builds on the first version, launched in 2019, drawing on lessons learned from implementation in over ten countries. It is written for government officials, development partners, and other practitioners who wish to achieve better outcomes from public spending on health.
In Kenya, the Council of Governors and the Ministry of Health, with support from WHO, have started applying the Toolkit, beginning with frontline health facility workers agreeing on the main service delivery problems they face every day.

Avec notre correspondante à Antananarivo ,  Aurélie Kouman
À   Madagascar  , le procès du drame d’Ambohimalaza se poursuit, cette affaire d’intoxication collective survenue le 14 juin 2025, lors d’une fête d’anniversaire près d’Antananarivo, où 35 personnes sont décédées, en majorité des jeunes. Le procès, retransmis en direct, s’est ouvert mercredi 18 novembre devant la Cour criminelle de la capitale malgache. Onze accusés sont jugés. Tous clament leur innocence.
Journée de visionnages
La journée du vendredi 20 novembre a été consacrée en partie au visionnage de plusieurs vidéos par la Cour. D’abord, des images de vidéosurveillance tournées sur le lieu de la fête. On y voit une femme se servir au buffet, avant le début des festivités. Selon l’accusation, c’est dans les plats de ce buffet qu’une poudre toxique aurait été versée. Le propriétaire des lieux dit reconnaître sur les images son épouse, morte dans le drame. La mère de l’organisatrice, elle, y reconnaît l’une des accusées, une cuisinière qui avait préparé les plats.
À lire aussi  Madagascar: des sources médicales contestent l'empoisonnement défendu par les autorités lors du drame d’Ambohimalaza
La cour a également diffusé des déclarations filmées pendant l’enquête. Une tradipraticienne, elle aussi accusée, affirme que cette cuisinière lui aurait demandé un produit pour rendre quelqu’un malade. La cuisinière, qui avait tout d’abord reconnu les faits, s’est ensuite rétractée à la barre, affirmant que ses aveux lui avaient été arrachés par les gendarmes.
Les familles veulent entendre ces gendarmes, des médecins réanimateurs et l’ancien ministre de la Santé, qui avait le écarté la thèse de l’intoxication en premier. Elles souhaitent que le parquet revienne sur les symptômes des victimes et leur prise en charge à l’hôpital, ce que les juges ont accepté.
À lire aussi  Madagascar: ouverture du procès du drame d'Ambohimalaza qui fit une trentaine de morts en 2025

items.title: RDC: les combats entre l'armée et le FRN provoquent de nouveaux déplacements de population dans le Sud-Kivu

original_payload.original_title: RDC: les combats entre l'armée et le FRN provoquent de nouveaux déplacements de population dans le Sud-Kivu
original_payload.original_body:
RDC: les combats entre l'armée et le FRN provoquent de nouveaux déplacements de population dans le Sud-Kivu
À l’est de la RDC, les affrontements entre l’armée congolaise et la rébellion du Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN) ont provoqué de nouveaux déplacements de population, notamment dans les territoires de Kalehe, Kabare, Uvira, et Fizi. Depuis lundi 16 novembre, l’armée congolaise aidée par les Wazalendo mènent des offensives dans plusieurs villages de Kalehe pour tenter de reprendre les zones passées récemment sous contrôle rebelle.
Publié le :  21/11/2026 - 08:09   Modifié le :  21/11/2026 - 08:32
2 min     Temps de lecture
Une vue aérienne des environs de Minembwe, dans la province du Sud-Kivu, à l'est de la République démocratique du Congo, le 7 octobre 2020.        AFP - ALEXIS HUGUET
Par :
RFI
Publicité
Aidées par l’armée burundaise et les Wazalendo, les forces armées de la RDC (FARDC) ont multiplié des frappes aériennes dans plusieurs villages des territoires d’Uvira et de Fizi, près de Minembwe, dans la province du Sud Kivu. La rébellion du Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN), emmenée par l’ancien président   Joseph Kabila  , accuse l’armée congolaise de bombarder écoles, structures sanitaires et habitations de civils à sur les hauts plateaux du Kivu.
À son tour, l’armée congolaise a accusé les rebelles de transformer les structures éducatives et sanitaires en dépôt d’armement et des munitions.
À lire aussi  Est de la RDC: l'armée congolaise à l'offensive face à des alliés du groupe politico-militaire FRN
Pour sa part, la société civile alerte que des milliers des déplacés vivent dans des conditions difficiles dans plusieurs villages de la province, et que leur situation humanitaire s’est aggravée. «  Leur situation, notamment à Bunyakiri, est particulièrement préoccupante  », s’inquiète Simon Weteshi Mihona, responsable du Club des Filles Reporters, une structure membre de la société civile basée à Bunyakiri.
Ce dernier souligne le manque d’abris, la nourriture insuffisante et un accès très limité aux services de base. «  De nombreux enfants ont abandonné l’école à la suite d’un déplacement forcé et se retrouvent privés de leur droit à l’éducation, exposés à différentes formes de vulnérabilité. Les femmes et les jeunes filles, quant à elles, sont particulièrement exposées au risque des violences sexuelles et aux grossesses non désirées  », appuie le membre de la société civile.
Nombre de ces déplacés sont hébergés dans des familles d’accueil qui, elles aussi, sont exposées aux nombreux combats qui font rage entre les belligérants. Selon Simon Weteshi Mihona, les conditions d’hygiène et d’assainissement sont alarmantes en raison «  du manque d’eau potable, de latrines adaptées et du manque de produits d’hygiène  ». Il appelle à une réponse humanitaire urgente dans une région souvent difficile d’accès pour les ONG.
À lire aussi  Est de la RDC: premiers contacts de la médiation du Qatar avec le groupe politico-militaire FRN

items.title: À la Une: Francophonie, retour sur les rapports de force diplomatiques entre Kinshasa et Kigali

original_payload.original_title: À la Une: Francophonie, retour sur les rapports de force diplomatiques entre Kinshasa et Kigali
original_payload.original_body:
La Une de la presse cette semaine à Kinshasa
À la Une:  Francophonie, retour sur les rapports de force diplomatiques entre Kinshasa et Kigali
Publié le :  21/11/2026 - 07:31
Écouter - 03:00
La presse kinoise revient ce vendredi sur les rapports de force diplomatiques entre Kinshasa et Kigali, avec deux dossiers qui interpellent: le maintien de Louise Mushikiwabo à la tête de l’Organisation internationale de la Francophonie et le projet de cinq pays européens d’installer au Rwanda un centre d’accueil pour migrants expulsés d’Europe. Les journaux s’intéressent également à la grève des armateurs fluviaux et au nouveau rebondissement judiciaire dans l’affaire opposant Moïse Katumbi et Raphaël Katebe Katoto.
Pascal Mulegwa.        © Anthony Ravera / Studio graphique FMM
Publicité
Commençons par la Francophonie. «  Kinshasa marque un point, Kigali gagne du temps  », titre    Le Potentiel  .  Le quotidien analyse le compromis trouvé à Phnom Penh, au   Cambodge  , autour de la succession de Louise Mushikiwabo. La secrétaire générale rwandaise reste en fonction pour douze mois supplémentaires, sans obtenir de reconduction immédiate. Pour le journal, ni Kinshasa ni Kigali ne peuvent revendiquer une victoire totale. La   RDC   a réussi à empêcher un nouveau mandat immédiat de la dirigeante rwandaise, mais n’a pas obtenu son départ sans délai. Le   Rwanda  , lui, conserve une année supplémentaire pour défendre ses intérêts. Une bataille d’influence donc, dont l’échéance est désormais repoussée à 2027.  Le Potentiel  souligne que «  dans les relations internationales, le temps est parfois une ressource stratégique  ».
Kinshasa s'indigne du flux des migrants vers Kigali
Autre dossier diplomatique, et cette fois-ci, la colère de Kinshasa est beaucoup plus manifeste. «  Double jeu des Occidentaux   : Kinshasa ne digère pas le flux des migrants vers Kigali  », titre  Forum des As .
Cinq pays européens, l'  Allemagne  , l’  Autriche  , le   Danemark  , la   Grèce   et les   Pays-Bas   envisagent de transférer au Rwanda des migrants déboutés du droit d’asile. Une initiative que la diplomatie congolaise juge difficilement compréhensible, au regard des accusations de soutien rwandais au Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN), nouvel avatar de l'  AFC/M23  . Kinshasa interpelle notamment le Danemark et la Grèce, qui ont voté la résolution 2773 du Conseil de sécurité exigeant le retrait des forces rwandaises du territoire congolais. La ministre des Affaires étrangères, Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner, appelle les Européens à faire preuve de «  cohérence  » : ne pas défendre une position à New York et en adopter une autre à Kigali.
Même indignation dans l' Ouragan . Le trihebdomadaire rapporte également les réserves de Human Rights Watch et d’Amnesty International sur les garanties en matière de droits humains. L’organisation britannique redoute notamment qu’un tel partenariat n’apporte des ressources financières et un avantage politique à Kigali.
Une contradiction diplomatique qui pose cette question : jusqu’où les intérêts migratoires européens peuvent-ils prendre le pas sur les engagements politiques et les principes de défense des droits humains ?
Dans un autre registre, les eaux congolaises sont à l’arrêt.  Maximum  revient sur la grève des armateurs qui protestent contre l’interdiction des embarcations en bois depuis le 15 novembre. Les exploitants réclament un moratoire de deux ans pour renouveler leurs flottes. Leur porte-parole, Jérémie Mwabikungu, juge irréaliste une transition en quelques semaines. Le journal rappelle toutefois que ces embarcations jouent un rôle essentiel dans l’approvisionnement de plusieurs provinces. Entre sécurité des passagers et continuité du transport fluvial, le gouvernement est attendu sur le terrain du dialogue.
Rebondissement judiciaire dans l’affaire Katumbi-Katebe
AfricaNews titre : «  Katumbi obtient gain de cause, le duel foncier contre Katebe renvoyé à mars 2027   » . La Cour de cassation a ordonné la réouverture des débats, à la demande de la défense de l’opposant. Celle-ci a notamment présenté une expertise belge portant sur sept documents attribués à Raphaël Katebe Katoto. Le tabloïd parle d’une victoire procédurale pour   Moïse Katumbi   contre son frère proche du pouvoir, «  mais certainement pas encore une victoire sur le fond  ».

items.title: TCN upgrades Bauchi substation to 330kV, targets 80,000 households

original_payload.original_title: TCN upgrades Bauchi substation to 330kV, targets 80,000 households
original_payload.original_body:
Business  TCN upgrades Bauchi substation to 330kV, targets 80,000 households
By  Abdulrahman Kadiri   ·   53 seconds ago   ·  4 min read
✓
✓
By Hope Ayodele
Bauchi, Nov. 20, 2026(NAN)The Minister of Power,  Joseph Tegbe, says the Federal Government remains committed to strengthening and upgrading electricity infrastructure nationwide.
Tegbe said this at the inauguration of the upgraded Bauchi Transmission Substation from 132kV to 330kV on Friday in Bauchi, by the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN).
He said the upgrade was aimed at strengthening electricity transmission capacity and improving power supply to Bauchi State and neighbouring communities.
He said that the intervention was expected to benefit more than 80,000 households and support growing economic activities in the state.
Tegbe said that the project represented a significant investment in strengthening the national electricity transmission network and improving its capacity to accommodate increasing demand.
He said that the facility, which previously operated with an installed capacity of 112.5MVA, had been upgraded with additional transformers to increase its transmission capacity.
Tegbe said that the upgrade involved the installation of two 100MVA 330/132kV power transformers, providing 300MVA upstream transmission capacity.
The minister said that two 60MVA 132/33kV transformers had also been installed, while the existing 60MVA transformer was retained, bringing the downstream capacity to 180MVA.
According to him, the project also includes a modern control room, two 330kV line bays, four 132kV bays, three additional 33kV outgoing feeders and upgraded control and protection facilities.
He said the improvements would enhance operational flexibility and provide a stronger platform for reliable electricity delivery.
The minister explained that the federal government was strengthening transmission infrastructure alongside efforts to expand electricity generation capacity.
He said that the approach was aimed at ensuring that the national grid could accommodate additional power generated in the country without unnecessary transmission constraints.
He noted that reliable electricity infrastructure was essential to supporting businesses, investment, public services and socioeconomic development.
Tegbe said that the investment aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s aspiration to position Nigeria towards a one-trillion-dollar economy.
He said that investments in electricity generation, transmission and distribution must translate into measurable economic and social benefits for Nigerians.
The minister also expressed concern over the increasing incidents of vandalism targeting electricity infrastructure across the country.
He condemned the destruction of transmission towers and other critical national assets, saying such activities had no justification.
Tegbe warned that vandalism disrupted businesses, livelihoods, working hours and family activities, while imposing additional costs on government to replace damaged infrastructure.
He urged Nigerians to protect electricity facilities and report suspicious movements, vandalism and unauthorised intrusion around such installations.
The minister reaffirmed the federal government’s commitment to strengthening the electricity sector and improving access to reliable power supply across the country.
Earlier, the Managing Director of TCN, Mr Sule Abdulaziz, said that the project had transformed the facility into a stronger transmission substation capable of handling increased electricity demand.
He explained that before the intervention, the substation operated at the 132/33kV level with an installed capacity of 112.5MVA.
The managing director said the intervention would strengthen bulk power delivery to the Jos Electricity Distribution Company (JEDC).
He listed the benefiting communities to include Ningi, Dass, Yankari, Nabardo, Gudum.Hausawa, Dabo Farms and Gubi amongst others.
He said the project was awarded in January 2021 and completed in June 2026.
According to him, it was executed by a joint venture involving MBH Power Ltd. and other members of the consortium with funding from the World Bank.
In his Goodwill message, Mr Riyas Cherayakkatt, representative of MBH Power Ltd. described the project as an important milestone in strengthening Nigeria’s transmission network.
He said that the company was proud to contribute to the development of the country’s power sector through the delivery of quality infrastructure.
He appreciated the federal government, Ministry of Power, TCN management, project consultants and other stakeholders for their support and cooperation.
In his remarks, the Emir of Bauchi, Dr Rilwanu Sulaiman, who was represented by the Waziri Bauchi, Alhaji Mohammed Uba-Kari, commended the federal government, Ministry of Power, TCN and other stakeholders for their contributions to the project.
The emir described the inauguration as an important milestone towards improving electricity infrastructure and promoting socioeconomic development in the benefiting communities.
He urged residents to regard the facility as a valuable public asset and take collective responsibility for its protection.
The royal father appealed to community members to report suspicious activities or anything capable of compromising the facility to the relevant authorities.
He assured the federal government and TCN of the people’s continued cooperation in protecting the infrastructure and ensuring its sustainable operation.
Speaking, Bauchi State Commissioner for Power, Alhaji Modibbo Abdulkadir, appreciated the federal government for improving power supply in the state.
He pledged the continued support of the state government to ensure that critical assets remained secure and protected.(NAN)
Edited by Stanley Nwanosike/Kevin Okunzuwa

items.title: Expert urges business owners to invest in talent development, retention

original_payload.original_title: Expert urges business owners to invest in talent development, retention
original_payload.original_body:
General News  Expert urges business owners to invest in talent development, retention
By  Folashade Adeniran   ·   6 minutes ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Lydia Chigozie-Ngwakwe
A real estate and sustainability expert, Mrs Chinwe Ajene-Sagna, has advised business owners to invest in talent development and adopt effective strategies for attracting and retaining skilled workers.
Ajene-Sagna, Managing Partner, Catalyst Realty Solution, made the call during a business clinic session/general meeting of the International Real Estate Federation (FIABCI), Nigeria Chapter, on Friday in Lagos.
The expert urged organisations to expose talented employees to new responsibilities and challenging projects to prepare them for leadership positions.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the meeting brought together professionals across the real estate value chain.
It had the theme, “Strengthening Networks, Advancing Real Estate, Building a Sustainable Future”.
She identified three approaches to talent acquisition as buying, borrowing and building talent.
She said that buying talent involved recruiting experienced professionals to fill critical positions, particularly where specialised skills and immediate results were required.
Borrowing talent, she said, involved engaging professionals on short-term contracts to handle specific projects or temporary business needs.
She described building talent as developing employees internally through training, structured career development and succession planning.
According to her, organisations should adopt a combination of the three approaches depending on their needs and stage of growth.
Ajene-Sagna said that building talent was particularly important for organisations seeking long-term growth, continuity and preservation of institutional knowledge.
She, however, noted that developing internal talent would require substantial investment in training and effective performance management.
The expert also advised organisations to conduct regular staff appraisals and use the process to identify employees’ strengths, weaknesses and career development needs.
She noted that performance management should involve setting clear corporate, departmental and individual targets so employees could understand what would be expected of them.
Ajene-Sagna added that employees who failed to meet established standards should be given opportunities to improve through a performance improvement plan before any decision on termination of their employments.
She also advised employers to review their staff welfare packages regularly particularly in view of the rising cost of transport and other living expenses.
According to her, providing support such as transport assistance and meals could help organisations to retain valuable employees.
On attracting young professionals, she recommended internship programmes as a means of identifying talented and committed graduates.
She said that organisations could use such programmes to assess young people’s skills, attitudes and readiness for the workplace.
Earlier, the President of FIABCI-Nigeria, Mr Ayodeji Odeleye, urged professionals in the real estate and building industry to strengthen professional relationships, share knowledge and embrace sustainable business practices for growth.
Odeleye said that there was still much work to be done in the industry, stressing the need for stakeholders to collaborate and build stronger professional networks.
He said that the association provided a platform for professionals, including interior decorators, architects, quantity surveyors and other players in the built environment, to connect and exchange ideas.(NAN)www.nannews.ng

items.title: FIABCI-Nigeria strengthens membership process to enforce participation

original_payload.original_title: FIABCI-Nigeria strengthens membership process to enforce participation
original_payload.original_body:
General News  FIABCI-Nigeria strengthens membership process to enforce participation
By  Folashade Adeniran   ·   6 minutes ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Lydia Chigozie-Ngwakwe
The International Real Estate Federation (FIABCI), Nigeria Chapter, has introduced changes to its membership process to encourage commitment, accountability and active participation.
The Vice-President of the chapter, Mrs Tolu Dima-Okojie, disclosed this at the chapter’s general meeting and business clinic held on Friday in Lagos.
Dima-Okojie said that prospective members would now be required to attend at least one physical event organised by FIABCI-Nigeria or its international body before applying for membership.
She added that referees of successful applicants would also be responsible for their conduct for two years after their induction.
According to her, each new member will be assigned a mentor to guide them and encourage their participation in the chapter’s activities for one year.
Dima-Okojie said the chapter would also encourage more members to participate in its committees to ensure that responsibilities were shared among members.
She urged members to become more involved in the federation’s activities, noting that they could only benefit fully from the association through active participation.
The vice-president also disclosed that the chapter inducted seven new members as part of efforts to strengthen its membership and promote greater participation in the real estate industry.
She said that six of the new members were physically present for the induction, while one participated from Germany.
She said that the chapter currently had 77 international members and 23 national members.
Two of the newly inducted members, Mrs Abiola Fadulu and Mr Isaac Ademola, expressed excitement about joining the federation.
Fadulu said joining FIABCI-Nigeria was an exciting step for her, adding that she looked forward to connecting with other real estate professionals and learning from their experiences.
She expressed eagerness to contribute to the industry, build meaningful relationships and explore opportunities for professional growth.
Similarly, Ademola, Lead Consultant and Senior Partner, Debola Ademola Consulting, described his induction as a rare privilege and a dream come true.
He said that he had looked forward to becoming a member of the global professional body and was excited to be part of its network.
Earlier, the President of FIABCI-Nigeria, Mr Ayodeji Odeleye, highlighted the chapter’s participation in the 2026 International Trade Mission in Taichung, Taiwan, where about 15 members attended a training programme.
In a goodwill message delivered virtually, the 2026/2027 FIABCI World President, Ms Lily Chang, congratulated the newly elected leadership of the Nigeria Chapter.
Chang expressed confidence that the new leadership would strengthen the chapter’s contribution to the global federation.
She also commended Nigerian members who participated in the international trade mission and stayed an extra day for an academic exchange programme at Feng Chia University in Taiwan.
According to her, such commitment to learning and sharing experiences would strengthen professional relationships and create opportunities for cooperation across countries. (NAN)

items.title: Sanwo-Olu pledges more housing opportunities for different income categories

original_payload.original_title: Sanwo-Olu pledges more housing opportunities for different income categories
original_payload.original_body:
General News  Sanwo-Olu pledges more housing opportunities for different income categories
By  Folashade Adeniran   ·   14 minutes ago   ·  4 min read
✓
✓
By Lydia Chigozie-Ngwakwe
In spite of ongoing investments in residential development, many Lagos residents still struggle to access decent and affordable housing, Gov. Babajide Sanwo-Olu said on Friday.
Sanwo-Olu, therefore, assured residents that his administration would continue to expand housing opportunities across different income categories.
He gave the assurance at the inauguration of 129 housing units at Brook’s Habitat, Abraham Adesanya, Ajah in Lagos.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the housing units were developed in partnership with Brook Assets and Resources Ltd.
Sanwo-Olu said, ‘’The expansion will be achieved through affordable housing schemes and financing arrangements aimed at making homeownership more accessible to residents, ‘’ he said.
The governor also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to expanding housing opportunities through public-private partnerships.
He said that the development was part of the government’s sustained efforts to increase the state’s housing stock, promote private-sector investment and provide decent residential accommodation for residents.
He said that the significance of the project went beyond the number of housing units delivered, describing it as part of his administration’s commitment to creating lasting infrastructure and sustainable communities.
According to him, the development demonstrates the importance of collaboration between government and credible private-sector investors in addressing the state’s growing housing needs.
Sanwo-Olu recalled that the original Abraham Adesanya Housing Estate was inaugurated in January 2001 by President Bola Tinubu, then governor of Lagos State.
He said that 25 years after the establishment of the estate, his administration was building on the existing foundation by creating more housing opportunities and improving the residential environment.
The governor disclosed that Brook’s Habitat comprised 129 residential units spread across 20 blocks on approximately 2.36 hectares of land.
He listed the facilities as 42 two-bedroom flats; 42 three-bedroom flats, with maid quarters and 45 three-bedroom terrace homes.
Sanwo-Olu said that the development, alongside 233 housing units inaugurated in the same axis in November 2025, had brought the total number of additional housing units delivered through two projects to 362.
He said that the estate was equipped with essential infrastructure, including internal roads, water supply facilities, electricity infrastructure, security arrangements, solar-powered streetlights and recreational facilities.
‘’Decent housing must go beyond the provision of residential buildings to include safe, functional and well-maintained surroundings.
“The housing needs of Lagos could not be met through government funding alone, given the state’s growing population and increasing demand for decent accommodation.
“The government has continued to encourage credible private developers to invest in the sector, with the state providing an enabling environment, land and necessary regulatory oversight.
“However, many residents still struggled to secure decent accommodation within their financial means,” the governor said.
Sanwo-Olu noted that construction activities created employment and business opportunities for engineers, artisans, building-material suppliers, transport operators and other service providers.
He commended the Lagos State Ministry of Housing, Brook Assets and Resources Ltd., consultants, contractors and other stakeholders for the successful completion of the project.
He advised prospective residents to take collective responsibility for maintaining the facilities and preserving the quality of the residential environment.
Also speaking, the Commissioner for Housing, Mr Moruf Akinderu-Fatai said that the state had provided people his renewal projects and the administration had built an ecosystem.
The commissioner said that the state had initiated and strengthened the Rent-to-Own scheme to open up home ownership to ordinary residents.
He commended Sanwo-Olu for his unwavering commitment to the delivery of affordable and decent housing.
He said: “You have provided the political will, political direction, and enabling environment that have made projects like Brook Habitat possible.
“Under your leadership, sir, housing has moved from rhetoric to reality. We have provided people, your renewal projects. This administration has built an ecosystem.
“We have initiated and strengthened the Rent-to-Own scheme to open up homeownership to ordinary residents. We have empowered LASRERA to protect citizens from fraudulent practitioners.”
The Managing Director, Brook Assets and Resources Ltd., Mrs Lanre Akinsola, said that the company overcame a four-year timeline and severe cash shortages to deliver the mixed housing estate and community commitments.
Akinsola recounted that work on the project began in April 2022 and was originally expected to take less than four years.
She said, “While the team achieved about 30 per cent completion within the first six months, progress stalled around October and November 2022 amid cash scarcity.
“This shifted public priorities away from buying homes. For roughly eight to nine months, construction halted completely”.
She applauded the state officials including the governor, the Ministry of Housing, and three permanent secretaries for guidance, firm oversight, and encouragement in spite of tough regulatory inspections. (NAN)

Business  NG-CARES: Lawmaker backs additional funding to lift vulnerable Nigerians out of poverty
By  Abdulrahman Kadiri   ·   14 minutes ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Emmanuel Ijikanmi
The Chairman, House Committee on Community and Social Development Agency/Nigeria Community Action for Resilience and Economic Stimulus (NG-CARES), Abubakar Kusada, has expressed support for the NG-CARES additional financing.
Kusada made this known at the closing / of the NG-CARES additional financing technical workshop in Abuja on Friday.
He described it as an opportunity to improve livelihoods and reduce poverty.
Kusada said that the additional financing would strengthen support for vulnerable households across the country.
He said the programme aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda and the government’s commitment to improving the welfare of vulnerable Nigerians.
Kusada urged implementing agencies to ensure that the additional funding reached those most in need, particularly underserved communities, female-headed households and persons living with disabilities.
He said that the farmers should receive timely agricultural inputs, while small businesses should benefit from interventions capable of sustaining and growing their incomes.
The lawmaker emphasised on the importance of measuring the programme’s impact through improvements in household welfare, food affordability and income stability.
Kusada also called for stronger collaboration among the Federal Government, World Bank, participating states and the National Assembly to ensure effective implementation.
Kusada said regular engagement with federal and state legislators would help address challenges and strengthen accountability.
The lawmaker urged implementing agencies to make eligibility criteria, application procedures and complaints channels accessible to Nigerians, including through local languages.
He further advocated transparent reporting of programme achievements across local government areas and wards to promote public confidence.
Kusada reaffirmed the committee’s readiness to work with programme partners to ensure that the additional financing delivered meaningful benefits.
He said that the committee would continue to support efforts aimed at improving livelihoods and lifting vulnerable Nigerians out of poverty.
The Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Budget and Economic Planning, Dr Deborah Odoh urged states to fast-track readiness requirements for effective participation in NG-CARES Additional Financing (AF).
She said delays in meeting programme requirements could affect families and businesses awaiting support.
The permanent secretary said the meeting developed action plans, timelines and milestones to strengthen implementation across various thematic areas.
These included food security, livelihood grants, basic services, social cash transfers, MSMEs support, fiduciary management and monitoring and evaluation.
Odoh said that the programme’s success should be measured by its impact on ordinary Nigerians rather than meetings held or funds disbursed.
According to her, families are expecting better opportunities and support to improve their livelihoods.
Odoh urged stakeholders to make NG-CARES AF more successful than its predecessor, NG-CARES 1.0, by building on its achievements and lessons.
She called for effective coordination, timely implementation, transparency and accountability among participating states and stakeholders.
The permanent secretary also commended the World Bank for its technical support and guidance throughout the meeting.
She commended state CARES coordinators, facilitators, resource persons and the Federal CARES Support Unit for their contributions.
Odoh said that the programme was not merely about implementation but about touching lives, restoring hope and providing families with a better future.
She urged stakeholders to translate the meeting’s resolutions into concrete actions to ensure sustainable benefits for Nigerians.
The World Bank Country Director for Nigeria, Mr Matthew Verghis, commended the Federal Government for their constant support to the programme.
Verghis, was represented by the World Bank Task Team Leader for NG-CARES, Dr Lire Ersado. (NAN)

Metro  FCC orders cancellation of NWRI recruitment over federal character breach
By  Funmilayo Adeyemi   ·   1 hour ago   ·  2 min read
✓
✓
By Grace Abe
The Federal Character Commission (FCC) has directed the cancellation of the recruitment of 58 staff members by the National Water Resources Institute (NWRI), Kaduna, over non-compliance with the Federal Character Principle.
FCC Spokesperson, Mr Ademola Lawrence, disclosed this in a statement issued in Abuja on Friday.
Lawrence explained that the cancellation followed a review of a report submitted by the commission’s monitoring officials, which established that the exercise failed to comply with the prescribed federal character balancing index.
He said that the commission was committed to ensuring equitable representation of all states of the federation and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).
He described the breach as a serious violation of the principles of fairness, equity and inclusiveness that underpin the federal character principle.
He insisted that recruitment into public institutions must reflect Nigeria’s diversity and not create imbalances that undermine the constitutional imperative of fair and equitable representation.
The spokesman added that the Federal Character Principle, as enshrined in Section 14(3) of the 1999 Constitution (as amended), was a constitutional requirement and not a mere administrative formality.
He noted that the provision placed a clear responsibility on public institutions to ensure fairness and balanced representation in appointments, recruitment and the distribution of opportunities across the country.
“The commission has directed the NWRI to cancel the entire recruitment exercise and commence the process afresh, with strict adherence to the prescribed federal character balancing index and all applicable requirements.
“The commission will not compromise its constitutional responsibility or overlook practices that undermine equitable representation in public institutions,” he said.
Lawrence stressed that every qualified Nigerian deserved a fair opportunity to access public employment, irrespective of state of origin or geographical location.
He reiterated the commission’s resolve to ensure that equity, fairness and national inclusion were reflected not merely in policies, but in the actual decisions and practices of government institutions. (NAN)

items.title: Turning asset recovery pledges into tangible wealth for African development ​‌‌​​​‌‍⁠⁠‍‍‍‍‍‌‌​‌‌​

original_payload.original_title: Turning asset recovery pledges into tangible wealth for African development ​‌‌​​​‌‍⁠⁠‍‍‍‍‍‌‌​‌‌​
original_payload.original_body:
Features  Turning asset recovery pledges into tangible wealth for African development    ​‌‌​​​‌‍⁠⁠‍‍‍‍‍‌‌​‌‌​
By  Kayode Adebiyi   ·   2 hours ago   ·  7 min read
✓
✓
​‌‌​​​  By Kayode Adebiyi
Each year, billions of dollars leave African economies through corruption and illicit financial flows.
Experts note that these funds could build hospitals, equip schools, pave roads, and support livelihoods across the 55 member states of the African Union.
Tracing, freezing, seizing, and returning stolen assets across different legal systems has long strained national laws and international cooperation.
In Abuja, however, Africa’s top anti-corruption officials, investigators, and financial intelligence experts met to change that reality for good.
Hosted by Nigeria’s Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) from November 17 to 20, the gathering marks the first General Assembly of the African Asset Recovery Practitioners’ Forum (AARP-F).
The event was convened under the auspices of the African Union Commission’s Department of Political Affairs, Peace and Security (AUC-PAPS) and the African Union Advisory Board Against Corruption (AUABC).
Participants said the theme of the assembly, “From Commitment to Action: Enhancing Africa’s Asset Recovery Architecture through Effective Implementation of the Common African Position on Asset Recovery (CAPAR)” was apt.
The gathering also transitioned AARP-F from an interim body into a permanent, practitioner-led continental institution armed with a substantive leadership council, four specialised working groups, a validated work plan and an operational budget.
Organisers said the four-day assembly marked a decisive institutional turning point for the continent.
At the opening event, Nigeria’s Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Chief Lateef Fagbemi, framed the mission not merely as a legal or technical exercise, but as a vital step toward national reform.
He said it was importantly as a fundamental question of justice and economic survival.
“Today, we gather not merely to discuss the recovery of stolen assets, but to confront a question of justice…
“How can a continent so richly endowed continue to be deprived of resources that should educate its children, equip its hospitals, build its infrastructure and secure its future?”
Drawing on an African proverb, the Fagbemi warned that “when the roots of a tree are being eaten away, its leaves cannot remain green for long”.
He noted that illicit financial flows eat directly at the roots of Africa’s development.
“Asset recovery is therefore not simply a technical exercise in tracing bank accounts or securing forfeiture orders. It is a struggle for accountability, economic sovereignty and the restoration of public trust.”
Fagbemi also underscored the same operational truth.
“Policies do not trace hidden assets; skilled practitioners do; declarations do not prepare mutual legal assistance requests; committed professionals do.
“And political will, however strong, must be translated into lawful investigation, effective prosecution, enforceable confiscation orders and accountable asset management,” he said.
That urgency was echoed by Dr Musa Aliyu, Chairman of the ICPC and Chair of the Forum’s Interim Steering Council, who emphasised the direct human cost of financial crimes.
“Every resource lost through corruption represents more than a financial loss; it is an opportunity denied to our people; resources that could otherwise support education, healthcare, infrastructure, security, employment and other essential public services.
“Behind every successfully recovered asset lies an opportunity to restore public value, strengthen institutions, advance justice and rebuild confidence in governance,” he said.
The Head of Development Cooperation at the German Embassy, Dr Karen Jansen, expressed concern over the enormous resources Africa continues to lose through illicit financial flows.
She said recovering these resources was imperative for financing development, improving citizens’ welfare and restoring public confidence in governance.
Jansen offered recommendations to strengthen Africa’s capacity to trace, freeze and recover stolen assets, highlighting the importance of international partnerships and sustained cooperation.
It is worth noting that the Abuja Assembly is the culmination of a deliberate, six-year continental effort anchored in the African Union’s Agenda 2063 and its broader governance and development financing priorities.
On Feb. 10, 2020, AU Heads of State and Government unanimously adopted the Common African Position on Asset Recovery (CAPAR) at their 33rd Ordinary Session in Addis Ababa.
The adoption, stakeholders acknowledged, built on the momentum of the 2018 African Anti-Corruption Year championed by Nigeria.
Rooted in the African Union Convention on Preventing and Combating Corruption, CAPAR established a unified continental policy framework built on four strategic pillars.
These are: detecting and identifying illicit assets; recovering and returning them to their countries of origin; transparently managing recovered assets; and strengthening international cooperation and partnerships.
Yet, as Kwami Senanu, Chairperson of the AUABC, reminded delegates in Abuja, policy declarations alone could not repatriate a single stolen dollar.
“Neither convictions, nor concept or position papers can by themselves stem illicit financial flows or help us to recover a single asset.
“What was clearly needed was an institution with the skill sets and experience to proactively follow through on our conviction.
“We need a group to constantly speak up on illicit financial flows and to actively pursue the return of assets.
“We need sustained action was needed and this required practitioners,” he said.
The journey to build that practitioner-led mechanism moved steadily over four years.
First mooted in Dakar, Senegal, in Sept. 2022 when the AUABC and AUC-PAPS convened asset recovery experts and prosecutors, the concept gained structural shape in Jan. 2024 in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania.
By May 2024 in Addis Ababa, Member States, Asset Recovery Inter-Agency Networks (ARINs), and prosecutors agreed upon and adopted the Forum Charter.
Three years after the initial vision, in April 2025, the AARP-F was unveiled in Nairobi, Kenya, with the signing of the Nairobi Declaration.
“This is Africa rising! Africa in action!” Senanu declared.
He praised Nigeria’s consistent leadership across the 55-member Union since proposing and sponsoring CAPAR in 2020.
“Today, this assembly turns an interim arrangement into a permanent platform, and it is a big win for us all,” he said.
However, some stakeholders, including Dr Abdullahi Yibaikwal, warn that, while African nations have steadily upgraded their domestic anti-corruption statutes, practitioners still confront formidable hurdles.
They say that criminal networks routinely exploit differences in national legal systems and opaque corporate structures that conceal beneficial ownership.
According to stakeholders, criminals also exploit delays in Mutual Legal Assistance, limited technical capacity and the prohibitive financial cost of litigating across multiple foreign jurisdictions.
Moreover,  Aliyu provided further insights
“Assets stolen from one country can be concealed, transferred or invested across several jurisdictions through complex financial arrangements designed to frustrate investigation and recovery.
“No country or institution can effectively confront these challenges in isolation.”
To ensure the newly institutionalised forum delivers measurable impact, he outlined six strategic priorities to guide the AARP-F’s work, including institutional development and governance to establish a credible, transparent leadership structure.
He also mentioned capacity building and professional development through specialised training and peer-to-peer knowledge exchange; and operational cooperation and information sharing to accelerate cross-border investigations and Mutual Legal Assistance.
“Strategic partnerships and international engagement with the AU, regional economic communities, and development partners such as GIZ and UNODC were also highlighted.
“Policy and legal development to harmonise domestic frameworks with regional and international standards; and sustainability and resource mobilisation to secure durable human, technical, and financial backing complete the list,” the ICPC chairman said.
Over the past year, the AUABC and its partners conducted targeted CAPAR capacity-building trainings across four African nations: Liberia, Eswatini, Chad, and Mauritius.
The Abuja sessions highlight this peer-to-peer approach, featuring practical cross-border asset-tracing lessons from Mauritius alongside case studies on recovering and managing confiscated wealth from Kenya and South Africa.
“These are African practitioners teaching African practitioners! This is the way to go; an African forum and model that focuses on practical experiences at the core,” Senanu noted.
At the assembly, Fagbemi admonished the practitioners that history would not judge them by the beauty of their declarations, but by the assets they recovered, the obstacles they removed and the difference they made.
Aliyu reinforced this demand for accountability, stating that real success would not be judged by the volume of meetings held or resolutions passed.
Instead, he emphasised that it depends on building strong partnerships, fostering meaningful cooperation, and delivering tangible results together.

✓
Kayode Adebiyi

items.title: Centre urges wider adoption of Kaizen to boost public sector productivity

original_payload.original_title: Centre urges wider adoption of Kaizen to boost public sector productivity
original_payload.original_body:
Metro  Centre urges wider adoption of Kaizen to boost public sector productivity
By  Funmilayo Adeyemi   ·   2 hours ago   ·  4 min read
✓
✓
By Mukhtar Sagir Dambatta
The National Productivity Centre (NPC) has urged public institutions to adopt continuous improvement practices to enhance productivity and service delivery.
The Director-General of NPC, Dr Baffa Dan’agundi, made the call at the centre’s third annual Kaizen Conference in Abuja on Friday.
The two-day conference, held from Thursday to Friday at Valencia Hotel, Wuse II, was organised with the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA).
It was under the theme ‘Driving Public Sector Productivity and Service Excellence Through Kaizen in Nigeria’.
Dan’agundi described Kaizen as an effective approach to tackling inefficiency and promoting lasting institutional transformation through small, consistent improvements.
He identified delays in file processing, unnecessary bureaucracy, resource wastage and inefficient workflows as challenges the approach could address.
He said public sector productivity should be measured by the quality, speed and transparency of services delivered to Nigerians.
The NPC Coordinator of Kaizen, Dr Adejoh David, urged participants to apply the knowledge acquired during the conference in their respective institutions.
Technical sessions examined Kaizen principles, workplace waste elimination (MUDA), the 5S workplace organisation system and the Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) cycle.
Others focused on process mapping, problem-solving and opportunities for introducing Kaizen into government institutions.
These included document processing, procurement, human resource administration, financial approvals, asset management and complaint handling.
A JICA Adviser, Ms Rika Aoki, shared international experiences, including Fukuoka City in Japan, where a “DNA movement” operates across 627 workplaces.
She also cited the Japanese Ministry of Finance’s internal portal for sharing Kaizen suggestions and Mauritius Prison Service’s 2025 Africa Kaizen Award.
Aoki said the Mauritius initiative reduced costs through quality circles involving staff and inmates.
She added that the Africa Kaizen Initiative, implemented by JICA and the African Union Development Agency, would run from April 2017 to April 2027.
One of the presenters, Dr Ehidiamhen Paul, recommended developing a National Kaizen Policy Framework to institutionalise the approach in Nigeria.
He also proposed Kaizen teams across ministries, departments and agencies, a three-year implementation roadmap and an annual excellence award.
Paul said NPC should lead technical capacity-building alongside the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation and the Bureau of Public Service Reforms.
He stressed the need to align Kaizen with existing public sector reforms to prevent duplication.
Another presentation highlighted improvements recorded at the Kaduna State primary healthcare warehouse following Kaizen’s introduction.
Figures attributed to Nigeria Health Watch showed that medicine stock-outs fell from 63 per cent to 11 per cent.
The figures also indicated that supply turnaround time dropped from about two weeks to between one and three days.
The conference attracted government officials, development partners and representatives of public institutions.
They included Mr Ishigame Keiji, Chief Representative of JICA Nigeria Office, and Mrs Olaolu Olaitan, Director of Inspectorate, Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment.
Others were Dr Samson Ebimaro of the Federal Ministry of Budget and Economic Planning and Mr Ogawa Izumi, a JICA Consultant.
Participants described the conference as educative and impactful.
Mr Jamilu Sani, a Senior Executive Officer in NPC’s Research, Consultancy and Business Development Department, said the programme deepened his understanding of workplace efficiency.
He said he would apply the knowledge and share it with colleagues, while calling for more capacity-building programmes.
Another participant, Mr Rossy, described the conference as an eye-opener that promoted discipline, accountability and continuous improvement.
He expressed confidence that proper implementation would improve institutional effectiveness and service delivery.
Rossy urged organisers to include Nigeria Customs Service officers in subsequent editions.
He also advocated introducing Kaizen principles into school curricula from primary to tertiary levels to promote discipline, responsibility and efficiency among young people. (NAN)

items.title: NATE, COREN Induct 150 Yabatech graduating students

original_payload.original_title: NATE, COREN Induct 150 Yabatech graduating students
original_payload.original_body:
Education  NATE, COREN Induct 150 Yabatech graduating students
By  Folashade Adeniran   ·   3 hours ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Kazeem Akande/Funmilola Gboteku
The Nigerian Association of Technologists in Engineering (NATE) and the Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria (COREN) on Thursday inducted 150 graduating engineering students of Yaba College of Technology (YABATECH), Lagos, into the engineering profession.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the induction, which featured oath administration, was held at the college in Yaba.
Speaking at the ceremony, the President of COREN, Prof. Sadiq Abubakar, represented by Mr Aramide Adeyoye, Chairman of COREN in Lagos State, said Nigeria currently had about 123 institutions offering engineering education, with over 662 programmes.
Abubakar said the resources, if managed diligently, could produce a large number of graduates in various fields, but questioned how skilful and competent the graduates were.
Adeyoye said COREN had developed a checklist in line with global best practices to guide engineering students from enrolment to graduation.
According to her, the checklist includes determination of carrying capacity for all engineering programmes, regulation of admission quotas, student indexing, adoption of 10 semesters in line with the Washington Accord benchmark.
It also includes mandatory induction of graduates, mandatory oath administration, mandatory Continuous Professional Development and mandatory annual renewal of practising licence.
She reassured the college management of COREN’s resolve to maintain the attainment of the Washington Accord benchmark through training, accreditation, assessment and other quality assurance activities.
Adeyoye also said COREN was ready to facilitate synergy between academia and industry through sabbatical leave of faculty to industry and adjunct appointment of industry captains to institutions.
She congratulated the graduating students, saying they would become pupil Engineering Technologists as soon as the oath was administered.
“The sky is your limit,” She said.
In his address, the NATE National President, Mr Dominic Udoatan, said the induction was in line with the mandate received from COREN on July 20, 2023, concerning induction and oath-taking of engineering graduating students in polytechnics and monotechnics.
Udoatan, represented by Mr Kayode Ibidapo, the National Secretary of NATE said the exercise was also in line with Nigeria’s status as a provisional signatory to the Washington Accord and its quest to join the Sydney Accord to internationalise the qualification of its engineering graduates.
Ibidapo described the event as proof of the growth of engineering and technology in the country and a collective desire of NATE and COREN to promote excellence, innovation and ethical practice.
He noted that the first of its kind in Nigerian polytechnics and monotechnics took place exactly a year ago at YABATECH, adding that the institution had been known for technical, vocational, engineering and technological education since 1947.
Also speaking, the Registrar of COREN, Mr Okorie Uche, represented by Mr Femi Adedotun, said the day marked a defining moment in the journey of the students.
Uche said engineering was more than equations, drawings and software, describing it as a sacred trust.
“Bridges must not fail. Buildings must not collapse. Systems must not endanger the public. The oath you are about to take is therefore not ceremonial, it is a covenant,” he said.
He urged the graduates to uphold competence, integrity, accountability and service to humanity, and to resist compromise and reject mediocrity.
In his remarks, the Rector of YABATECH, Mr Ibraheem Adedotun, congratulated the students for successfully joining the field of professionals.
Adedotun advised them to be passionate about the job, tap experience from professionals and seek mentorship to stay ahead of their mates.
One of the graduating students, Emmanuela Osagie, said she would like to further her studies abroad, focusing on robotics engineering in the next five years.(NAN)
Edited by Kevin Okunzuwa

items.title: Colleagues celebrate late journalist Nwanne’s legacy

original_payload.original_title: Colleagues celebrate late journalist Nwanne’s legacy
original_payload.original_body:
General News  Colleagues celebrate late journalist Nwanne’s legacy
By  Folashade Adeniran   ·   3 hours ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Glory Akpan
Colleagues and associates of Chukwuebuka  Nwanne,  the General Manager, Abuja and Northern Operations of The Guardian Nigeria, have celebrated his contributions to journalism, Nollywood and community development.
They paid the tributes at a candlelight session held in his honour, recalling his commitment to professionalism, friendship and positive change.
The  News Agency of Nigeria (NAN)  recalls that Nwanne passed on on Oct. 3, after a protracted illness.
Colleagues at the candlelight session of Late Chuks Nwanne
A former President of the Directors Guild of Nigeria, Fidelis Duker, described Nwanne as one of the journalists whose contributions to Nollywood and the wider entertainment industry deserved greater recognition.
Duker said his professional work, alongside that of other entertainment journalists, helped promote Nollywood and attract international attention to the industry.
He urged stakeholders to recognise the contributions of journalists who helped build the sector.
Colleagues at the candlelight session of Late Chuks Nwanne
Similarly, filmmaker Bond Emeruwa described Nwanne as an important figure in Nollywood’s publicity and promotion.
Emeruwa said filmmakers depended on entertainment journalists to publicise their productions, noting that their reports helped create awareness about Nigerian films.
He urged media practitioners and industry stakeholders to preserve the history of those who contributed to the development of Nollywood.
Also speaking, the News Editor of The Guardian, Tope Olaiya, described Nwanne as a close friend, brother and professional colleague whose relationship with him spanned more than 15 years.
Olaiya, who said Nwanne was his best man at his wedding, recalled that their friendship went beyond professional responsibilities in spite of their different ethnic backgrounds.
He described him as a lively personality who brought colleagues together through music and social activities.
Olaiya added that Nwanne was passionate about community development and improving the lives of people around him.
“We miss him so greatly. It is sad to see him go at this time, but God knows best,” he said.
In her tribute, Ijeoma Thomas-Odia, Editor, Guardian Woman at The Guardian Newspapers,  described Nwanne as a mentor whose guidance and leadership shaped her journalism career.
Thomas-Odia said she met him when she joined The Guardian, adding that he helped develop her confidence, resilience and professional skills.
She described him as an exceptional editor who prioritised professionalism over personal relationships.
“He was an editor who did not need to like you before he could work with you. He taught me a lot of leadership skills that have shaped who I am today,” she said. ( NAN )www.nannews.ng
Edited by Vivian Ihechu

original_payload.original_body:
N’Djaména : La mairie renforce l’encadrement des stations de lavage
admin
novembre 21, 2026
1 minutes de lecture
69 vues
Le maire de la Ville de N’Djaména, Senoussi Hassana Abdoulaye, a rencontré, ce vendredi 20 novembre 2026, les responsables des stations de lavage d’engins opérant dans la capitale. La rencontre a porté sur les conditions d’installation et d’exploitation de ces établissements.
Au cours des échanges, les promoteurs ont été sensibilisés à l’obligation d’obtenir une autorisation préalable pour exercer leurs activités et de respecter les règles fixées par la municipalité.
La mairie entend ainsi mieux organiser le secteur, mettre les installations existantes en conformité et éviter les implantations anarchiques. Des contrôles seront également renforcés, avec des mesures administratives prévues en cas de non-respect des règles.
À travers cette initiative, la municipalité souhaite contribuer à l’amélioration du cadre urbain et à la préservation de la salubrité publique.

items.title: Harry Kane to miss ‘a few months’ after injury as Bayern Munich draw

original_payload.original_title: Harry Kane to miss ‘a few months’ after injury as Bayern Munich draw
original_payload.original_body:
England football captain Harry Kane will miss the “next few months” after tearing a ligament in his left ankle during Bayern Munich’s 1-1 draw against Cologne on Friday.
Kane was taken down in the area by Cologne defender Joel Schmied, who reached Michael Olise’s low cross first but knocked into the Ballon d’Or winner’s left leg in his follow-through at the back post.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items    list 1 of 4  Can Mauricio Pochettino save Manchester United?
list 2 of 4  Leaders Arsenal travel to beleaguered Newcastle as Premier League returns
list 3 of 4  ‘Total error of judgement’: Drone operator removes United training footage
list 4 of 4  Tashima says Balogun red card row at World Cup prompted FIFA presidency bid
end of list
Kane writhed in pain. Although he gingerly got back to his feet and initially continued playing, he soon hobbled off the field with two physiotherapists after treatment.
A club statement on X said: “Harry Kane suffered a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle in Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga home match against Köln on Friday evening. This was confirmed by an examination by Bayern Munich’s medical department. The 33-year-old will therefore be out for the next few months.”
Kane is the undisputed star of Bayern. Since joining from Spurs in 2023, he has scored 156 goals in 161 competitive fixtures and won two Bundesliga titles and the German Cup.
He became the first Englishman to  win the Ballon d’Or  in 25 years last month and, two weeks ago,  signed a new contract  with Bayern that will keep him in Bavaria until June 2029.
The night was supposed to be a happy one for Bayern, who welcomed coach Vincent Kompany back to the dugout a month after he collapsed while watching the reserve squad train.
However, Kompany saw his team go behind after just 11 minutes when winger Mikey Moore, on loan from Tottenham, started and finished a counterattack.

items.title: Three US citizens among 4 convicted in Honduras over sex-trafficking case

original_payload.original_title: Three US citizens among 4 convicted in Honduras over sex-trafficking case
original_payload.original_body:
A court in Honduras has convicted four people, including three United States citizens, of criminal association in connection with the 2022  disappearance of a woman  whose whereabouts are still unknown.
The Public Ministry said on Friday that it would request the maximum jail term of 10 years for each defendant after they were found guilty of recruiting women into a sex-trafficking ring. The next hearing is due to take place on December 9.
Recommended Stories

list 3 of 3  Verdict delayed in Honduras sex-trafficking case linked to disappearance

The ministry also said it would appeal the court’s decision to acquit US citizens Harold Green and William James Murdock of human trafficking.
They were found guilty of the lesser crime of criminal association, along with fellow US national Gary Lee Johnston and Honduran national Gustavo Trejo.
Woman’s disappearance
Angie Pena disappeared on January 1, 2022, while jet skiing by the Caribbean island of Roatan, off the northern coast of Honduras.
She was a 22-year-old university student when she went missing and police initially suspected she had drowned. However, her family believed she had been abducted and demanded an investigation.
A trafficking investigation was later launched after the jet ski Pena had used was found in Belize, about 90 nautical miles (170 kilometres) away from Roatan.
Investigators later found she had fallen prey to a sex-trafficking network called “Delta Teams” that has since been dismantled. The Attorney General’s Office determined minors were among the trafficked victims.
“The Public Ministry [Attorney General’s Office] obtained a guilty verdict against four members of the network known as Delta Teams for the violation of criminal association,” the prosecutor’s office said on X.

items.title: Journée mondiale de la télévision : l’ONAMA envisage de lancer une deuxième chaîne en 2027

original_payload.original_title: Journée mondiale de la télévision : l’ONAMA envisage de lancer une deuxième chaîne en 2027
original_payload.original_body:
À l’occasion de la Journée mondiale de la télévision, célébrée chaque 21 novembre, le directeur de la télévision à l’Office national des médias audiovisuels (ONAMA), Souleyman Djabo, revient sur l’histoire de la télévision au Tchad, ses évolutions et les défis auxquels elle fait face. Il annonce également le projet de lancement d’une deuxième chaîne thématique à l’horizon 2027.
Proclamée en décembre 1996 par l’Assemblée générale des Nations Unies, la Journée mondiale de la télévision met en lumière le rôle de ce média dans l’information, la communication et le partage des connaissances.
Au Tchad, l’histoire de la télévision nationale remonte au 10 décembre 1987. Selon Souleyman Djabo, directeur de la télévision à l’ONAMA, sa création répondait notamment à un besoin de communication autour des grands événements organisés dans le pays et dans la sous-région. «  Au Tchad, c’est dans les années 1987, plus précisément le 10 décembre 1987, que la télévision nationale a été créée  », rappelle-t-il.
Lire aussi :  Tchad : la télévision nationale lance son premier journal télévisé en langue des signes
Il appuie que les autorités de l’époque avaient jugé nécessaire de mettre en place ce média pour accompagner les grands rendez-vous accueillis par le pays. «  C’était à l’occasion des grands événements de la sous-région. Les autorités de l’époque ont jugé utile de communiquer. C’est vrai que la radio existait bien avant, mais ils ont voulu que ce soit la télévision qui vienne appuyer ces grands événements qui se déroulent ici dans notre pays  », précise-t-il.
Évoquant les premières années de la télévision tchadienne, Souleyman Djabo se souvient d’une époque où les images et le son étaient suivies sur différents canaux. «  Je me rappelle très bien, on suivait les images aux écrans et le son à la radio  », raconte-t-il.
Lire aussi :  Tchad : le projet de Télévision numérique terrestre présenté au public
De la télévision nationale à l’Office national de radio et télévision du Tchad (ONRTV), puis à l’ONAMA, la structure a connu plusieurs évolutions institutionnelles et techniques.
Pour son directeur, les progrès technologiques ont permis à la télévision tchadienne de franchir un nouveau cap.
«  Aujourd’hui, on est au même niveau avec les plus grandes chaînes de télévision, en matière technique. Aucune télévision de la sous-région ne peut nous dépasser. Donc, je pense qu’aujourd’hui, avec la nouvelle technologie, on est au même niveau que les plus grandes chaînes du monde  », affirme-t-il.
Cependant, malgré ces avancées techniques, la production de contenus demeure un défi majeur pour la chaîne publique. Le directeur souligne notamment les difficultés liées à l’insuffisance des moyens de production.
«  Les défis sont multiples. Pour la chaîne publique que nous sommes, je pense que notre grand défi, c’est le contenu du programme. Le contenu du programme pose problème parce que nous n’arrivons pas à produire suffisamment, faute de moyens  », reconnaît-il.
Dans la perspective de diversifier son offre audiovisuelle, l’ONAMA envisage néanmoins le lancement d’une deuxième chaîne en 2027. Celle-ci devrait accorder une place particulière aux préoccupations de la jeunesse, des femmes et aux questions environnementales.
«  D’ici 2027, si tout se passe bien, nous comptons lancer une deuxième chaîne qui doit prendre en compte la jeunesse, les femmes et l’environnement. Ce sont des thématiques qui sont très en vogue à l’heure où nous sommes. Avec le temps, on va créer d’autres chaînes thématiques  », annonce Souleyman Djabo.
Le Tchad compte aujourd’hui huit chaînes de télévision à savoir Tchad infos TV, Sahara TV, Electron TV, Tchad 24, Toumaï TV, Al Nassr, Manara TV et l’unique télévision publique.

Il annonce également le projet de lancement d’une deuxième chaîne thématique […] L’article Journée mondiale de la télévision : l’ONAMA envisage de lancer une deuxième chaîne en 2027 est apparu en premier sur Tchadi
