Later on Saturday, the IRGC also claimed bringing down an MQ-1 drone over Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, the 19th such downing.
There was no immediate comment by the US military.
The incidents come days after the US and Iran engaged in  direct, tit-for-tat strikes , against a backdrop of increasing Iranian attacks on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz, the vital waterway through which one-fifth of the world’s oil and gas passed in peacetime.
Launched by the US and Israel on February 28, the war has killed thousands of people and severely disrupted shipping, pushing global energy prices higher and spreading to countries across the region.
The US and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding in June, but it was never fully implemented because of disagreements over freedom and security of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, with attacks resuming periodically since July. In August, The Washington Post reported that the US had lost 45 MQ-9 drones, or about 25 percent of its fleet at a cost of more than $1.3bn, during combat operations in Iran.
original_payload.original_summary: Iran reiterates conditions for Hormuz reopening as US slaps sanctions on four Iranians it says acted as 'oil trustees'.

original_payload.original_body:

Cette descente cible particulièrement les gros porteurs et les camions de transport dont de nombreux chauffeurs ont pris l’habitude d’installer des projecteurs additionnels, des rampes LED ou des feux de forte intensité non réglementaires.
L’opération fait suite à de multiples plaintes de citoyens et d’automobilistes, régulièrement aveuglés et mis en danger lors des croisements nocturnes.

items.title: Tchad : le Collectif 2M dresse son bilan des deux premières années du mandat présidentiel

original_payload.original_title: Tchad : le Collectif 2M dresse son bilan des deux premières années du mandat présidentiel
original_payload.original_body:
A l’approche de la mi-mandat du président de la République, le Collectif 2M « Marchons avec Mahamat », dirigé par Senoussi Hassana Abdoulaye, a organisé, ce jeudi 19 novembre 2026 à N’Djaména, une rencontre consacrée à l’évaluation des deux premières années de gouvernance du Maréchal Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno. Plus d’une centaine d’associations et d’organisations de la société civile ont pris part aux échanges, qui ont été sanctionnés par la signature d’une tribune sur le bilan présidentiel et les attentes pour les trois prochaines années.
Évaluer les engagements pris par le chef de l’État, examiner les réalisations enregistrées et identifier les défis qui restent à relever. Tels étaient les principaux objectifs de cette rencontre initiée par le Collectif 2M « Marchons avec Mahamat ».
Prenant la parole, le président du collectif, Senoussi Hassana Abdoulaye, a rappelé que les organisations ayant soutenu le Maréchal Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno lors de l’élection présidentielle du 6 mai 2024 ont également un rôle à jouer dans le suivi de la mise en œuvre de son projet de société. Il a notamment insisté sur la nécessité de reconnaître les avancées réalisées, tout en relevant les insuffisances qui appellent des réponses concrètes.
Dans leur déclaration, les responsables du collectif ont salué les initiatives engagées en faveur de la refondation de l’État, du renforcement des institutions républicaines, de la cohésion sociale et de la stabilité nationale. Ils ont, par ailleurs, réaffirmé leur soutien au chef de l’État, tout en plaidant pour une accélération de la mise en œuvre de ses engagements.
Les discussions ont également permis de passer en revue plusieurs préoccupations majeures des populations. La sécurité, l’emploi des jeunes, l’accès à l’eau potable et à l’électricité, l’éducation, la décentralisation et le renforcement des services sociaux de base ont notamment été abordés.
Une attention particulière a été accordée à l’insertion professionnelle des jeunes, à leur accompagnement ainsi qu’à la recherche de solutions durables aux conflits intracommunautaires. Le pouvoir d’achat a également figuré parmi les préoccupations soulevées, notamment en ce qui concerne les attentes des populations autour de la subvention des denrées alimentaires.
À l’issue des échanges, les associations et organisations participantes ont signé une tribune présentant leur appréciation des deux premières années du mandat présidentiel et formulant des recommandations pour les trois prochaines années.
À travers cette initiative, le Collectif 2M entend poursuivre son accompagnement du chef de l’État, tout en appelant à la concrétisation des engagements pris et à des réponses davantage adaptées aux attentes des populations tchadiennes.

items.title: Salamat : concertation autour de la gestion du parc national de Zakouma et de la réserve du Bahr Salamat

original_payload.original_title: Salamat : concertation autour de la gestion du parc national de Zakouma et de la réserve du Bahr Salamat
original_payload.original_body:
Le délégué général du gouvernement auprès de la province du Salamat, Ahmat Choua Rozi, a présidé, ce vendredi 20 novembre 2026, à Djouna, une rencontre consacrée au processus d’élaboration des plans d’aménagement et de gestion (PAG) du parc national de Zakouma (PNZ) et de la réserve de faune du Bahr Salamat (RFBS), ainsi qu’à leurs règlements intérieurs respectifs. Djouna est une localité située à environ 85 kilomètres au sud d’Am-Timan.
Ces assises s’inscrivent dans le cadre des tournées sous-préfectorales de sensibilisation et de concertation autour de l’élaboration et de la validation des documents de gestion des deux aires protégées.
L’élaboration et la validation de ces plans relèvent de la responsabilité conjointe du ministère en charge de l’Environnement et d’African Parks Network (APN). À ce titre, l’implication des autorités de tutelle dans le pilotage technique et institutionnel du processus est jugée essentielle.
Lire aussi :  Le gouvernement installe le Comité technique chargé de l’élaboration des Plans de développement touristique du Parc national de Zakouma et de la Réserve naturelle et culturelle de l’Ennedi
Pour le directeur général du Grand Écosystème du parc national de Zakouma, Cyril Pélissier, l’objectif est de favoriser une appropriation collective du processus d’élaboration des PAG par l’ensemble des parties prenantes. À cet effet, une méthodologie de travail a été élaborée par l’Unité de gestion du parc (UGP), avec l’appui de consultants.
Cette démarche prévoit notamment la collecte et l’analyse des données, ainsi que l’identification des problématiques liées à la gestion des aires protégées.
Elle comprend également l’organisation d’ateliers provinciaux d’information des parties prenantes, des réunions avec l’équipe technique d’appui pour faire le point sur l’avancement du processus participatif et recueillir les avis, ainsi que des tournées sous-préfectorales auprès des communautés riveraines.
Lire aussi :  Interview : ‘’Lutter contre le braconnage, c’est l’affaire de toutes et tous’’, Cyril Pélissier, directeur du parc national de Zakouma
Ces consultations visent à mettre les communautés au courant des enjeux et des options envisagées avant toute prise de décision, afin de favoriser un dialogue éclairé et de faciliter la conclusion d’accords librement consentis.
L’objectif général de ces tournées est de présenter à l’ensemble des parties prenantes les enjeux, les thématiques et les options liés à la conservation et à la gestion durable du parc national de Zakouma et de la réserve de faune du Bahr Salamat.
De manière spécifique, ces consultations doivent permettre d’examiner, d’enrichir et de valider, de façon participative et concertée, les propositions relatives à l’aménagement, à la gouvernance et à la gestion durable des deux aires protégées.
Elles portent notamment sur la composition, les attributions et l’ancrage territorial des structures concernées, ainsi que sur l’identification et la validation des outils nécessaires à la mise en œuvre des PAG et à l’application des règlements intérieurs.

items.title: Moundou : le tribunal renvoie au 27 novembre le verdict sur la légalité de la mise en place de l’exécutif communal

original_payload.original_title: Moundou : le tribunal renvoie au 27 novembre le verdict sur la légalité de la mise en place de l’exécutif communal
original_payload.original_body:
L’affaire opposant six conseillers communaux de la Convention tchadienne pour la paix et le développement (CTPD) à la Commune de Moundou, au sujet de la mise en place de l’actuel exécutif communal, a été examinée ce vendredi 20 novembre 2026 par la chambre administrative du Tribunal de grande instance (TGI) de Moundou. À l’issue des débats et des plaidoiries, le tribunal a mis l’affaire en délibéré au 27 novembre prochain.
L’audience publique a été marquée par des échanges nourris entre les avocats des deux parties. Me Guillaume Allaramadji Rirongarti, conseil des six conseillers communaux requérants, conteste la régularité de la procédure ayant conduit à l’installation de l’actuel exécutif communal. De son côté, Me Gadnodji Prosper, avocat de la Commune de Moundou, défend la légalité de cette mise en place.
Lire aussi :    Moundou : l’exécutif communal sur la sellette
Un désaccord sur la cessation des fonctions de l’ancien maire
Au cœur du contentieux se trouve la légalité du procès-verbal de la session extraordinaire du 16 juin 2026, qui a consacré la mise en place du nouvel exécutif communal.
Pour Me Guillaume Allaramadji Rirongarti, l’ancien maire, Djékaoussem Elon Bondo, demeure légalement le maire de Moundou. Selon lui, aucun acte administratif ou juridique régulier n’a officiellement mis fin à ses fonctions avant l’installation de son successeur, Béassemda Emmanuel.
Une position contestée par Me Gadnodji Prosper. L’avocat de la Commune soutient que l’ancien maire aurait accepté son départ, notamment en refusant de signer le procès-verbal ayant acté la mise en place du nouvel exécutif. Il invoque également une situation exceptionnelle qui aurait nécessité une intervention urgente.
En réponse, Me Guillaume Allaramadji Rirongarti s’appuie sur la loi organique n° 014/CNT/2024 relative à l’organisation des collectivités autonomes. Il dénonce ce qu’il considère comme une violation des règles de compétence et de procédure.
De son côté, le maire actuel a justifié le changement intervenu à la tête de la municipalité par les difficultés qu’aurait connues la gestion précédente. Il a notamment évoqué des accusations de détournement et de corruption, un manque de collaboration, une gestion qu’il qualifie de chaotique ainsi qu’un niveau d’endettement important.
Lire aussi :    Moundou a un nouvel exécutif communal
Les requérants dénoncent plusieurs irrégularités
Dans leurs conclusions en contre-réplique, les six conseillers communaux de la CTPD ont développé plusieurs arguments pour demander l’annulation du procès-verbal contesté.
Le premier concerne la compétence de l’autorité habilitée à mettre fin aux fonctions du maire. S’appuyant sur les articles 117, 119 et 123 de la loi organique n° 014/CNT/2024, les requérants soutiennent que la démission d’office relève du représentant de l’État dans la commune, tandis que la révocation doit être prononcée par décret motivé pris en Conseil des ministres.
Ils affirment qu’aucun acte du représentant de l’État déclarant l’ancien maire démissionnaire d’office, ni aucun décret de révocation, n’a été produit au dossier.
Les requérants contestent également la régularité de la convocation de la session extraordinaire du 16 juin 2026. Selon eux, la Commune n’a pas versé au dossier l’arrêté préfectoral de convocation. Ils estiment en outre que le délai légal de sept jours prévu pour convoquer le Conseil communal n’aurait pas été respecté. Ils font valoir que, selon les explications de la partie adverse, la convocation serait intervenue le jour même de la session.
Autre point soulevé : l’absence du représentant de l’État à cette séance et les conditions de désignation de la personne chargée de présider les travaux. Les requérants contestent notamment la présidence assurée par le maire adjoint, estimant que les règles de remplacement fondées sur l’âge des conseillers communaux n’auraient pas été respectées.
Les six conseillers mettent également en cause les conditions du vote ayant conduit à la désignation du nouvel exécutif communal. Se référant à l’article 116 de la loi organique, ils rappellent que l’élection du maire doit se dérouler au scrutin secret et à la majorité absolue des voix.
Or, selon leurs conclusions, le procès-verbal litigieux fait plutôt état d’une répartition consensuelle et inclusive des postes entre différentes formations politiques, sans préciser clairement les modalités du scrutin, le nombre de suffrages exprimés ni la majorité effectivement obtenue.
La question du quorum constitue un autre motif de contestation. Les requérants relèvent que le nom du conseiller Mbaidessemel Dionadii figure sur le procès-verbal avec la mention « P.O », laissant entendre qu’il aurait été représenté par procuration. Ils rappellent que l’article 111 de la loi organique prévoit, selon leur interprétation, que seuls les conseillers physiquement présents sont pris en compte et que les procurations ne sont pas valables.
Enfin, les demandeurs estiment que les accusations de mauvaise gestion formulées contre l’ancien exécutif ne peuvent, à elles seules, justifier le non-respect des dispositions légales encadrant la cessation des fonctions d’un maire. Ils soutiennent que les mécanismes spécifiques prévus notamment par les articles 121 à 123 auraient dû être engagés si des fautes étaient reprochées à l’ancien maire.
Lire aussi :    Moundou : le parti CTPD dénonce la désignation de Beassemnda Emmanuel comme maire de Moundou
Une demande d’annulation du procès-verbal
Au terme de leurs conclusions, les six conseillers communaux demandent au tribunal de rejeter les arguments de la Commune et de constater l’absence d’un acte légal mettant fin aux fonctions de l’ancien maire.
Ils sollicitent également la reconnaissance des irrégularités qu’ils dénoncent dans la convocation, la présidence et le déroulement de la session extraordinaire du 16 juin 2026, ainsi que dans les conditions du scrutin et du quorum.
En conséquence, ils demandent l’annulation du procès-verbal de cette session extraordinaire et de toutes les opérations de mise en place du nouvel exécutif communal qui en découlent. Ils réclament enfin la condamnation de la Commune de Moundou aux dépens.
Un climat de tensions autour du contentieux
En attendant le délibéré prévu le 27 novembre 2026, cette affaire continue de susciter des réactions dans le paysage politique local.
En coulisses, certains soutiens de l’actuel exécutif communal accusent le président de la CTPD, Laoukein Kourayo Médard, de faire cause commune avec l’ancien exécutif pour déstabiliser l’équipe municipale en place. Des accusations rejetées par des sources proches de la CTPD, qui dénoncent plutôt des manœuvres sur les réseaux sociaux visant, selon elles, à influencer le cours de la procédure judiciaire.
La décision du Tribunal de grande instance de Moundou, attendue le 27 novembre, devra apporter un éclairage juridique sur la régularité de la mise en place de l’actuel exécutif communal.

original_payload.original_title: Ngone Saar dévoile « ADN », un pont musical entre tradition et modernité
original_payload.original_body:
CULTURE
Ngone Saar dévoile « ADN », un pont musical entre tradition et modernité
Le collectif tchadien Ngone Saar a présenté son deuxième album, « ADN ». Composé de 18 titres, ce projet artistique met à l'honneur les valeurs culturelles et l'héritage du pays.
Alwihda Info
21 nov. 2026
Le collectif Ngone Saar a présenté, vendredi 20 novembre, son deuxième album de 18 titres intitulé « ADN ». Dévoilé lors d'une conférence de presse, ce projet artistique se veut un hommage aux valeurs culturelles du Tchad.
Pour le groupe, cet opus va au-delà d'une simple production musicale. Il ambitionne de raconter l'identité tchadienne et de célébrer l'héritage national. À la croisée de la tradition et de la modernité, l'album est le fruit d'un travail de recherche approfondi.
Les artistes expliquent avoir multiplié les échanges avec des sages et des aînés pour recueillir leurs conseils. Cette démarche de transmission intergénérationnelle a guidé la conception de l'œuvre.
Le collectif garde le secret sur le contenu musical précis, mais donne rendez-vous au public le 27 novembre prochain à Pili Pili pour un concert de présentation.

items.title: Afrique du Sud: des femmes en colère manifestent pour réclamer justice face aux féminicides

original_payload.original_title: Afrique du Sud: des femmes en colère manifestent pour réclamer justice face aux féminicides
original_payload.original_body:
Afrique du Sud: des femmes en colère manifestent pour réclamer justice face aux féminicides
Il y a un an, à la veille du lancement du G20 en Afrique du Sud, des milliers de femmes participaient à un sit-in silencieux à travers le pays pour dénoncer les féminicides dont les taux sont parmi les plus élevés au monde. Les manifestantes avaient alors obtenu que ces violences soient classées comme catastrophe nationale. Un an plus tard, jour pour jour, elles sont de nouveau dans la rue, ce samedi 21 novembre, pour dénoncer une situation toujours dramatique et réclamer davantage de moyens concrets.
Publié le :  21/11/2026 - 14:31
A travers les rues de Johannesburg, en Afrique du Sud, quelques centaines de personnes suivent un cercueil noir et violet. Il symbolise les femmes victimes de féminicides, une manifestation pour dénoncer une situation toujours dramatique et réclamer davantage de moyens concrets, le 21 novembre 2026.        AFP - ILARIA FINIZIO
Par :
RFI
Avec notre correspondante à Johannesburg,   Joséphine Kloeckner
À travers les rues de Johannesburg, quelques centaines de personnes suivent un cercueil noir et violet. Il symbolise les femmes victimes de féminicides.
Dans le cortège, des survivantes et des familles de victimes qui, pour beaucoup, attendent toujours que justice soit rendue. Après 15 minutes de silence, pour 15 femmes tuées chaque jour dans le pays, la ministre des Femmes, de la jeunesse et des personnes en situation de handicap est venue, en personne, recevoir une lettre de demandes de l’organisation Women for Change.
Toujours pas d'objectifs ni d'actions tangibles
Son discours - dans lequel elle assure l’implication du gouvernement dans la lutte contre les violences de genre - est vite étouffé sous les huées des femmes en colère qui réclament de passer de la parole aux actes. La foule s’empare du micro, de nombreuses femmes racontent, en larmes, les violences dont elles ont été victimes et les proches qu’elles ont perdu.
Un an après la classification des violences de genre comme catastrophe nationale, le plan d’action du gouvernement ne présente toujours pas d’objectifs chiffrés, ni d’actions tangibles, malgré l’annonce de fonds supplémentaires, il y a un mois.

items.title: Firm Blames Anambra Power Crisis On National Grid, Says It Received About 107mw Despite 1000mw Demand

original_payload.original_title: Firm Blames Anambra Power Crisis On National Grid, Says It Received About 107mw Despite 1000mw Demand
original_payload.original_body:
The FirstPower Electricity Distribution Company Limited has blamed the worsening electricity supply across Anambra State on declining national grid generation and inadequate power allocation.
The company said that its network received less than 107 megawatts (MW) on every day of the past week, despite the state requiring about 1,000MW to meet its energy needs.
The electricity distribution company made this known in a statement issued on Friday, November 20, 2026, by its Head of Communications, Izunna Okafor, amid growing concerns among residents, businesses and industries over persistent power shortages and inconsistent electricity supply across the state.
The company said the situation was part of wider challenges confronting Nigeria's electricity sector, particularly fluctuations in power generation and reduced allocations from the national grid to the country's 11 electricity distribution companies (DisCos).
“Recent reports and data from the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) show that electricity generation has been fluctuating considerably, with a noticeable decline in the volume of energy available for distribution to the country's 11 electricity distribution companies (DisCos),” Okafor stated.
“Yesterday, November 19, 2026, national grid generation was reported to have dropped from 3,743 megawatts (MW) around midnight to 3,179MW by 6 a.m., and later increasing marginally to 3,180MW by 6 p.m.
“The development left the 11 distribution companies with a total allocation of approximately 2,885MW to be shared among themselves, further constraining electricity supply across the country.”
Okafor added, “In that allocation of 2,885MW, Abuja DisCo received the highest allocation of 551MW, followed by Ikeja DisCo with 366MW, Ibadan DisCo with 340MW, and Eko DisCo with 339MW.
“Port Harcourt DisCo received 279MW, Benin DisCo 230MW, EEDC (which FirstPower operates under) got 220MW, Kano DisCo 173MW, Kaduna DisCo 167MW, and Jos DisCo 146MW, while Yola DisCo got 74MW. This shows the level of general drop in supply across the country, as a result of the drop in generation.
“Down here at the level of FirstPower's distribution network in Anambra State, the situation is reflected in the combined electricity allocation received through the four TCN interface stations serving the company: Awada, GCM, Nibo and Agu-Awka.”
The company said that its operational records showed that the network received 90.52MW on November 13, increasing to 95.50MW on November 14 and 106.73MW on November 15.
However, according to the company, the allocation subsequently crashed to 64.34MW on November 16 before rising to 80.13MW on November 17 and 81.37MW on November 18.
It further declined slightly to 80.55MW on November 19 before recovering to 91.33MW as of 7:16am on Friday.
FirstPower acknowledged that although the latest allocation represented an improvement over the previous day, it remained significantly below the 106.73MW received on November 15.
The company said the fluctuations had made it difficult to maintain consistent electricity supply across Anambra State.
The admission comes against the backdrop of Governor Chukwuma Soludo's disclosure at a recent investment roundtable organised by the Anambra State Electricity Regulatory Commission (ASERC) that the state requires approximately 1,000MW of electricity but currently receives only about 120MW at most.
FirstPower's latest figures indicate that its distribution network has not received up to 107MW on any single day within the reviewed week, further highlighting the gap between the state's electricity requirements and the power currently available to consumers.
In a bid to address the shortfall, FirstPower said that it recently signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Greenewable Energy Limited for the development of 100MW of embedded electricity generation in Anambra State.
The agreement, the company said, was signed during the investment roundtable organised by ASERC, with FirstPower describing the proposed project as part of efforts to diversify its energy sources and increase electricity availability for residents.
The company, however, did not provide a specific timeline for the commencement or completion of the proposed 100MW project.
FirstPower also sought to clarify its position within the electricity value chain, stressing that it does not generate the electricity it distributes to consumers.
The company likened its operations to those of a distributor who cannot supply goods beyond the quantity received from a manufacturer.
While acknowledging the difficulties faced by households, businesses and industries, FirstPower appealed to residents to exercise patience and understanding, particularly as economic and commercial activities increase ahead of the festive season.
It assured customers that it would continue working with EEDC, TCN, NISO and other relevant stakeholders to improve electricity allocation and stabilise supply across its distribution network.
The company also promised to manage available electricity more efficiently and equitably while monitoring developments in the national power sector.

items.title: Indian National Sentenced To Nearly 20 Years In US For Plotting To Assassinate Sikh Leader

original_payload.original_title: Indian National Sentenced To Nearly 20 Years In US For Plotting To Assassinate Sikh Leader
original_payload.original_body:
A 55-year-old Indian national, Nikhil Gupta, has been sentenced to 235 months (nearly 20 years) in a United States prison for his role in a plot allegedly orchestrated by an Indian government employee to assassinate Sikh separatist leader and US-based attorney Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York City.
Gupta was sentenced on Friday by US District Judge Victor Marrero in the Southern District of New York after pleading guilty in February 2026 to murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire and conspiracy to commit money laundering.
The US Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York announced the sentence, describing the case as an assassination conspiracy allegedly directed by an employee of the Indian government.
According to the US Justice Department, Gupta worked with Vikash Yadav, an alleged Indian government employee, to arrange Pannun's murder on American soil in 2023.
Yadav was identified in court documents as an employee of India's Cabinet Secretariat, which houses the country's foreign intelligence agency, the Research and Analysis Wing (RAW).
Prosecutors said Yadav recruited Gupta in May 2023 to organise the killing of Pannun, a US citizen of Indian origin who leads a US-based organisation advocating for the independence of Punjab, a northern Indian state with a large Sikh population.
Pannun has been an outspoken critic of the Indian government and has advocated for the establishment of an independent Sikh state known as Khalistan. The Indian government has banned him and his separatist organisation from operating in India.
The court documents revealed that Gupta approached an individual he believed to be a criminal associate to help recruit a contract killer.
However, the individual was actually a confidential source working with the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), who subsequently introduced Gupta to an undercover DEA officer posing as a hitman.
Prosecutors said Yadav, through arrangements brokered by Gupta, agreed to pay the undercover officer $100,000 to assassinate Pannun.
On June 9, 2023, Gupta and Yadav allegedly arranged for an associate to deliver $15,000 in cash to the undercover officer as an advance payment for the killing.
The US Justice Department further disclosed that Yadav supplied Gupta with sensitive personal information about Pannun, including his residential address in New York, telephone numbers and details of his daily movements.
Gupta subsequently passed the information to the undercover officer and regularly updated Yadav on the operation, including providing surveillance photographs of the intended victim.
Investigators said Gupta repeatedly instructed the undercover officer to carry out the assassination as quickly as possible but warned him not to execute the operation around the time Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi was scheduled to visit the United States on an official state visit beginning June 20, 2023.
The plot reportedly took a more urgent turn following the killing of another prominent Sikh separatist leader, Hardeep Singh Nijjar, in Canada.
On June 18, 2023, masked gunmen shot Nijjar dead outside a Sikh temple in British Columbia, Canada.
Nijjar, like Pannun, was a prominent advocate of the Khalistan movement and a vocal critic of the Indian government.
According to prosecutors, Gupta contacted the undercover officer on June 19, the day after Nijjar's killing, and disclosed that Nijjar had also been a target.
He reportedly told the undercover officer that there were "so many targets" and that, following Nijjar's killing, there was "now no need to wait" before carrying out the assassination of Pannun.
Gupta was arrested in the Czech Republic on June 30, 2023, at the request of US authorities and was subsequently extradited to the United States in June 2024.
Announcing the sentence, US Attorney Jamie McDonald said the punishment reflected the seriousness of Gupta's actions and warned that American authorities would pursue individuals involved in planning violence against US citizens, regardless of where they operated.
"While in India, Gupta helped to methodically plan the victim's murder, believing he was beyond the reach of a U.S. court. But Gupta was wrong," McDonald said.
He added that the sentence demonstrated the US government's commitment to prosecuting individuals involved in violent plots on American soil.
Gupta was also ordered to pay a $300 special assessment in addition to his prison sentence.

items.title: Tinubu Appoints Ex-Lagos Commissioner Dabiri To NASS Service Commission

original_payload.original_title: Tinubu Appoints Ex-Lagos Commissioner Dabiri To NASS Service Commission
original_payload.original_body:
President Bola Tinubu has approved the appointment of former Lagos State Commissioner for Youth and Social Development, Agboola Lukman Dabiri, as the South-West representative on the National Assembly Service Commission (NASC).
Dabiri replaces Taiwo Olukemi Oluwa, who resigned from the commission on March 30, 2026, to contest the 2027 general election for the Irewole/Isokan Federal Constituency in Osun State.
The appointment was announced on Friday in a statement issued by the President’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga.
According to the statement, Dabiri previously served as Commissioner for Youth and Social Development in Lagos State.
He also served as Mandate Secretary for Economic Planning, Revenue Generation and Public-Private Partnership in the Federal Capital Territory.
Onanuga said the appointment was part of Tinubu’s efforts to ensure effective representation and inclusivity in the National Assembly Service Commission.
“The appointment is part of the President’s efforts to ensure effective representation and inclusivity in the National Assembly Service Commission,” the statement read.
The National Assembly Service Commission is responsible for the appointment, promotion and discipline of staff of the National Assembly.
Established under Section 157 of the 1999 Constitution, the commission plays a key role in overseeing the administration and personnel management of the National Assembly.
Dabiri’s appointment fills the South-West position previously occupied by Oluwa, who stepped down to pursue her political ambition ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The development comes as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 polls, with several public office holders and political actors positioning themselves for elective offices.

items.title: 2027: Tinubu May Win Only Two States In Credible Polls – Baba-Ahmed

original_payload.original_title: 2027: Tinubu May Win Only Two States In Credible Polls – Baba-Ahmed
original_payload.original_body:
The National Chairman of the Peoples Redemption Party, Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, has predicted that President Bola Tinubu may win only two states in the 2027 presidential election if the exercise is free, fair and credible.
Baba-Ahmed said growing dissatisfaction with the Tinubu administration over economic hardship, insecurity and the rising cost of living could cost the All Progressives Congress victory in the next general election.
He made the prediction during an interview on ARISE News on Friday, insisting that Nigerians across the country, and not only those in the North-West, were increasingly unhappy with the president's performance.
He said, “If the elections are free and fair, President Tinubu, I repeat, will not win this election. Nigerians as a whole, not just Northwest, will reject him because he has not performed anywhere near what they expected.
“I said if the elections are credible, free and fair in 2027, President Tinubu is unlikely to win more than two states. I didn’t even say anything about the Northwest. I said in the country.”
The PRP chairman said his assessment was based on his party's interactions with ordinary Nigerians and their experiences under the current administration.
According to him, the government has concentrated more on retaining political power than addressing the country's economic and security challenges.
“The Tinubu administration was more interested in just being in power than actually fixing problems in the country,” he said.
Baba-Ahmed said the opposition party regularly engaged citizens to understand their concerns, adding that the growing hardship was evident in conversations with Nigerians.
He said, “We don’t just assume things. We mix with them. We don’t give them money. We don’t have the money that APC has to give them. So, we engage with them. We follow their lives. We follow their opinions. We are in touch with their sentiments.”
On the opposition's efforts to challenge the APC in 2027, Baba-Ahmed said the PRP had been involved in coalition discussions from the beginning.
He listed the Peoples Democratic Party, Social Democratic Party, African Democratic Congress, Allied Peoples Movement and Nigeria Democratic Congress among the political parties involved in the discussions.
He said the coalition had identified two major objectives: removing the APC from power and presenting Nigerians with a credible alternative.
“We are providing Nigerians a credible option to the APC, the most credible option to the APC. And we have a very comfortable expectation that we will win this election because Nigerians will reject from top to bottom. They will reject APC,” he said.
The opposition leader also raised concerns about political violence and alleged restrictions on opposition parties' campaign activities ahead of the election.
He claimed that opposition parties were facing difficulties accessing campaign venues and mounting billboards, while warning that attacks and disruptions of political activities could undermine the electoral process.
Baba-Ahmed also dismissed suggestions that northerners who voted for Tinubu in 2023 would be hypocritical if they withdrew their support in 2027.
He argued that voters had the democratic right to reconsider their political choices based on the performance of an elected government.
“If the north elected Tinubu in 2023, it was the rights of northerners who felt that Tinubu was a better candidate than Obi and Atiku. And they have the same right now to reject Tinubu. There’s nothing hypocritical about this. That is what politics is all about,” he said.
Baba-Ahmed, who previously served as Special Adviser on Political Matters to Tinubu, also defended his decision to leave the administration, saying he became convinced that the government was not serious about governance.
“I left the administration because I saw no evidence that President Tinubu’s administration was serious about governance,” he said.
Tinubu won the 2023 presidential election on the platform of the APC, defeating Atiku Abubakar of the PDP and Peter Obi, who contested under the Labour Party.
The 2027 election is expected to witness another contest involving the ruling party and opposition politicians seeking to build a united political front against the president.

items.title: Tinubu's Praise Singer Rarara Attacked, Beaten By Worshippers At Abuja Central Mosque

original_payload.original_title: Tinubu's Praise Singer Rarara Attacked, Beaten By Worshippers At Abuja Central Mosque
original_payload.original_body:
President Bola Tinubu’s praise singer, Dauda Kahutu, popularly known as Rarara, has been attacked and beaten by a group of angry worshippers at the Abuja National Mosque.
In a video obtained by SaharaReporters, the incident occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, as the singer was reportedly confronted by worshippers who descended on him and physically assaulted him within the mosque premises.
The footage shows several worshippers surrounding Rarara and beating him before some individuals intervened to rescue him from the attackers.
He was subsequently taken to security operatives at the mosque for protection following the attack.
At the time of the incident, Rarara was dressed in an Agbada. He was also seen holding a cap bearing an inscription and logo associated with President Tinubu.
The video shows the singer being overwhelmed by the angry crowd before some worshippers stepped in to shield him and help him reach security personnel.
In November 14, 2026, SaharaReporters reported thatTinubu was booed by some angry worshippers and residents at the Shehu Shagari Central Mosque in Area 1, Garki, Abuja, shortly after observing Friday prayers.
The incident occurred last week Friday as the President's convoy prepared to leave the mosque, with several people heard chanting slogans expressing opposition to his administration.
According to reports, video clips obtained from the scene showed some members of the crowd chanting “Ba mayi, ba ma so”, a Hausa expression translated as “We don't want you; we don't support you”.
Others reportedly chanted “Tinubu Must Go”, a slogan associated with opposition to the President's re-election bid ahead of the 2027 general elections.
An eyewitness who attended the prayers said that the protest might have been triggered by restrictions imposed on worshippers because of Tinubu's visit.
The source, who requested anonymity, said the President arrived at the mosque at about 1:49pm, by which time access to the premises had already been restricted.
According to the eyewitness, security operatives prevented people from entering the mosque after the President arrived, while roads leading to the premises were blocked.
Some security personnel were also reportedly stationed on the mosque's perimeter fences as part of the security arrangements.
The restrictions allegedly continued after the prayers, with worshippers prevented from leaving until the President's departure.
The eyewitness said some of those affected expressed their frustration through chants directed at Tinubu as his convoy prepared to leave.
Another source at the mosque also attributed the reaction partly to what was described as excessive security arrangements.
“People were stopped from entering the mosque after the president had entered. Several people were stuck outside,” the source said.
The source added that the booing started from the area where people had been barricaded, suggesting that the restrictions contributed to the frustration among worshippers.

items.title: Naira Slides To ₦1470/$ On Parallel Market Amid Forex Crisis

original_payload.original_title: Naira Slides To ₦1470/$ On Parallel Market Amid Forex Crisis
original_payload.original_body:
The naira has continued to lose ground against the United States dollar, with businesses reportedly paying about ₦1,395 for a dollar at the official foreign exchange window on Friday, November 20, 2026, while the parallel market rate climbed to between ₦1,465 and ₦1,470.
The latest depreciation has raised fresh concerns among business operators and financial market participants, who say the continued volatility is putting additional pressure on importers, manufacturers and ordinary Nigerians already struggling with rising operating costs.
Sources who spoke to SaharaReporters on Friday expressed concerns over the Federal Government's failure to provide clear answers and a convincing strategy for addressing the worsening foreign exchange situation.
They specifically questioned the economic management of President Bola Tinubu's administration and the response of Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) Governor, Olayemi Cardoso, stating that the authorities must explain why the naira is weakening despite previous interventions and assurances that the government's economic reforms would stabilise the currency.
The official exchange rate has also recorded a significant increase in recent weeks.
Data cited by market sources showed that the official rate stood at approximately ₦1,346.26 per dollar on October 30, 2026, before rising to ₦1,376.58 on November 19, according to the CBN's reported average.
The figure represented a further depreciation of about ₦13 within a single day, with transactions reportedly reaching as high as ₦1,397.
By Friday morning, November 20, businesses were reportedly paying approximately ₦1,395 per dollar through the BMATCH trading window, while the parallel market rate hovered between ₦1,465 and ₦1,470.
The latest figures indicate that the official rate has weakened by nearly ₦49 per dollar compared with its October 30 level, while the gap between the official and parallel markets has widened to approximately ₦90.
The difference has raised questions about the effectiveness of the current foreign exchange management system, particularly as businesses say the rates published by the CBN do not always reflect the prices at which they can actually secure dollars.
Another major concern raised by market participants is the country's declining foreign exchange reserves and the reported volume of dollars being supplied by the CBN to support the market.
Nigeria's external reserves reportedly fell from a recent peak of $55.26 billion in late October to approximately $54.87 billion by November 20.
The decline has occurred despite the CBN's reported intervention of about $1.98 billion in the foreign exchange market in October.
Market data cited in the analysis showed that the naira still depreciated by approximately 1.31 per cent during the month, raising questions about the sustainability and effectiveness of the interventions.
Financial market analysts have also warned that the official foreign exchange market is becoming increasingly dependent on dollar supplies from the CBN, rather than consistent inflows from exporters, investors and other private-sector sources.
Sources familiar with developments in the foreign exchange market told SaharaReporters that businesses across several sectors are suffering significant financial losses as the naira continues to depreciate.
Importers are among the worst affected, with the latest exchange rate movement adding approximately ₦49 million to the cost of purchasing every $1 million worth of imported goods compared with the end of October.
Business operators say the additional cost is threatening profit margins, particularly for companies that had already agreed on prices with customers before the latest depreciation.
Manufacturers are also facing higher expenses for imported raw materials, industrial equipment, spare parts and other production inputs.
The situation could force some companies to increase the prices of their products, reduce production or slow down operations.
Amid the growing pressure, market participants and affected business operators are calling on the Tinubu administration and the CBN to take urgent steps to address the crisis.
They want the CBN to ensure timely foreign exchange allocations for genuine import transactions, particularly those involving essential commodities such as food, medicines and other critical goods.
Other recommendations include publishing a transparent strategy to increase dollar inflows through exports, diaspora remittances and foreign investment, while reducing excessive dependence on interventions from the country's external reserves.
They further called for measures to narrow the gap between the official and parallel market exchange rates and restore confidence in the foreign exchange market.
More than three years into the administration, businesses and households continue to face the consequences of exchange rate volatility, with operators demanding clearer explanations and more effective measures from the authorities.

items.title: All Eyes On INEC Chairman Prof Amupitan: Electoral Workers’ Welfare, Poor Pay, Inducement Risks & Need For Proper Remuneration Before Next Election, By Daniel Nduka Okonkwo

original_payload.original_title: All Eyes On INEC Chairman Prof Amupitan: Electoral Workers’ Welfare, Poor Pay, Inducement Risks & Need For Proper Remuneration Before Next Election, By Daniel Nduka Okonkwo
original_payload.original_body:
Across Nigeria’s electoral landscape, the credibility of the ballot rests heavily on the shoulders of a large, often inadequately remunerated and overstretched workforce, a vulnerability that deserves far greater attention ahead of the 2027 general elections. Long before a single vote is cast across the country’s 176,846 polling units, persistent welfare and payment concerns, ranging from unimplemented reviews of electoral-duty honoraria and allowances to delayed and incomplete payments to ad hoc personnel, raise serious questions about the financial security of those entrusted with administering the democratic process. As Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) Chairman Professor Joash Ojo Amupitan prepares to oversee the January 16 and February 6, 2027 elections under a proposed ₦873.78 billion budget, public debate has largely focused on BVAS technology, electronic transmission of results, and security deployments.
Yet INEC’s own post-election assessment and documented complaints by electoral workers in Anambra, Enugu, Lagos, and Ondo reveal another institutional concern: the consequences of inadequate remuneration, delayed payments, and unresolved welfare obligations. In Anambra State, for instance, more than 150 ad hoc personnel protested at INEC’s headquarters in Awka in May 2023 over outstanding election allowances. One protester alleged that workers had received only ₦3,000 as a feeding allowance while ₦14,000 remained outstanding for each of the two election exercises, claiming that more than 300 personnel were affected. Similar payment complaints were subsequently documented among electoral workers in Lagos in 2023, Enugu in the aftermath of the 2019 general elections, and Ondo following the November 2024 governorship election. More significantly, INEC's own 2023 General Election Report acknowledged that inadequate honoraria for Presiding Officers and Assistant Presiding Officers caused discouragement and created room for temptation and inducement. With the national voters' register now exceeding 103 million, the central question is whether INEC's leadership and the Federal Government will finally translate their budgetary provisions, policy announcements, and welfare commitments into prompt, fair, and verifiable payments before the 2027 elections, or leave the integrity of the electoral process exposed to the economic vulnerabilities of the very personnel entrusted with protecting it.

La Confédération africaine de football va créer une Coupe d’Afrique des nations féminine des moins de 17 ans. La décision a été approuvée samedi 21 novembre par son comité exécutif réuni à Abuja, au Nigeria, sous la présidence de Patrice Motsepe. L’instance a également ouvert le processus de candidature pour l’organisation de la première édition.
Cette nouvelle épreuve doit offrir aux jeunes joueuses africaines un rendez-vous continental régulier et renforcer leur parcours vers les sélections seniors. Les associations membres peuvent désormais se positionner pour accueillir la compétition inaugurale.
Jusqu’ici, les sélections féminines U17 du continent disputaient principalement des éliminatoires donnant accès à la Coupe du monde de la catégorie. La création d’une CAN dédiée ajoute donc une compétition finale africaine à ce niveau d’âge, avec un pays hôte et un titre continental propres.
Le comité exécutif a profité de sa réunion au Nigeria pour ouvrir un second appel à candidatures, consacré à la CAN féminine senior 2028. Les fédérations intéressées disposent de trois semaines pour transmettre leur dossier au secrétariat de la CAF.
La CAN féminine 2028 est programmée en mars et avril, tandis que ses éliminatoires doivent commencer en avril 2027. Les deux décisions élargissent le calendrier continental proposé aux footballeuses, depuis les catégories de jeunes jusqu’au niveau senior.

Des centaines de baraques et de petites boutiques adossées à la clôture du parc de véhicules d’occasion de Sèkandji ont été démolies lors d’une opération engagée par la mairie de Sèmè-Podji, avec l’appui de la Police républicaine. Le dégagement, entamé plusieurs jours avant le samedi 21 novembre 2026, concerne les voies et les abords de ce site situé dans l’arrondissement d’Agblangandan.
Le long de la clôture du parc, les installations commerciales ont laissé place à des gravats. Les engins ont notamment parcouru des ruelles donnant accès au marché automobile, où des commerçants exerçaient dans des constructions de fortune.
Des exploitants cités par Banouto contestent les conditions de l’intervention. Une commerçante affirme ne pas avoir été prévenue avant la destruction de sa boutique. D’autres personnes, installées à l’intérieur des allées, ont pu évacuer leurs marchandises et récupérer une partie de leurs matériaux avant le passage du bulldozer.
Une source policière citée par le média présente l’opération comme une libération d’espaces publics occupés sans autorisation. Elle évoque également des préoccupations de sécurité autour du parc automobile.
Benoît Saïzonou, chef du quartier de Sèkandji-Houéyogbé, indique ne pas avoir été associé au déclenchement des démolitions. Il affirme que le secteur du parc est régulièrement évoqué lors de réunions sur l’insécurité et situe l’intervention dans un mouvement plus large de dégagement des espaces publics à Agblangandan.
La commune avait déjà été concernée en octobre par  une autre opération d’identification de constructions sur des emprises réservées à l’écoulement des eaux . Celle-ci portait notamment sur des habitations d’Agblangandan, pour lesquelles la direction générale du Développement urbain avait annoncé des sommations et des délais avant toute libération des logements occupés. Autour du parc de Sèkandji, il s’agit cette fois d’installations commerciales en bordure des voies.
Selon la source policière interrogée par Banouto, les opérations de dégagement doivent se poursuivre dans d’autres ruelles de Sèkandji. Le chef de quartier signale aussi des interventions similaires dans plusieurs localités de l’arrondissement d’Agblangandan.

La dotation globale de la Ligue des champions africaine atteint 19,6 millions de dollars. La Confédération africaine de football (CAF) a détaillé cette enveloppe samedi 21 novembre, à Abuja, au Nigeria, lors de la présentation de ses comptes annuels 2026.
Le vainqueur de la compétition reçoit désormais 6 millions de dollars, contre 2,5 millions en 2021. Le ministère béninois des Affaires étrangères a annoncé, samedi 21 novembre 2026, le déploiement d’une mission gouvernementale d’assistance consulaire au Mali et au Burkina Faso, où se trouvent des ressortissants ayant quitté la Guinée après les opérations contre l’orpaillage illégal. Le collectif « SEOH Dégage » a annoncé une marche pacifique pour dimanche 22 novembre 2026 à Ross-Béthio, dans le nord du Sénégal. Il réclame le départ de la Société d’exploitation d’ouvrages hydrauliques (SEOH) et de l’Office des forages ruraux (OFOR), qu’il met en cause dans les difficultés d’approvisionnement en eau de la commune.
Lors d’un point de presse rapporté vendredi par Seneweb, Anta Gaye, membre du collectif, a demandé que la Société nationale des eaux du Sénégal (SONES) prenne le relais. Les membres du mouvement estiment que le développement urbain de Ross-Béthio nécessite une organisation différente de celle actuellement appliquée aux ouvrages hydrauliques ruraux.
Les revendications concernent aussi le stockage. Anta Gaye évalue à 300 mètres cubes la capacité du château d’eau actuel, jugée insuffisante pour la commune. Le collectif demande la construction de deux autres châteaux d’eau et dénonce la qualité de l’eau distribuée dans les foyers.

Ils avaient remis au sous-préfet de l’arrondissement de Ndiaye un mémorandum réclamant notamment le départ de SEOH, selon le journal EnQuête+.

La nouvelle marche, annoncée pour le dimanche 22 novembre à Ross-Béthio, doit porter les demandes de changement d’opérateur et de renforcement des installations.

Archive du 9 février 2026, exercice Dynamic Front 26, Cincu (Roumanie). Crédit Capt. Regina Koesters / US Army / DVIDS / Wikimedia Commons, domaine public américain, image recadrée.
Partager

La France a commandé 50 000 obus d’artillerie de 155 mm à KNDS Ammo France et financera la moitié d’un investissement destiné à augmenter la production du site de La Chapelle-Saint-Ursin, dans le Cher. Dans une annonce publiée le 20 novembre 2026, la  Direction générale de l’armement  (DGA) fixe à 150 000 obus par an la capacité visée d’ici 2029.
Ces deux chiffres recouvrent des engagements différents. Les 50 000 munitions constituent une commande pour l’armée de Terre, dont les livraisons sont prévues en 2029 et 2030. Les 150 000 obus correspondent à une capacité de production annuelle future, et non au volume de ce contrat. La commande avait été passée le 12 novembre.
Le site du Cher disposait d’une capacité annuelle de 30 000 obus de 155 mm en 2022. Elle a atteint 60 000 en 2025, selon le ministère des Armées. La cible de 2029 représenterait ainsi deux fois et demie le niveau de 2025. Sur la même période de réorganisation industrielle, le délai de fabrication annoncé a été ramené de 21 à 12 mois.
La montée en cadence reposera sur la construction d’une nouvelle unité de coulée d’explosifs et de deux unités dédiées à l’usinage et au ceinturage des munitions de gros calibre. L’État et KNDS France financeront l’investissement à parts égales. Le groupe précise que le projet industriel a été reconnu d’intérêt national majeur par un décret publié le 29 juin 2026.
Les obus de 155 mm équipent notamment les systèmes d’artillerie CAESAR, utilisés par les forces françaises et des armées partenaires. L’extension de la capacité doit répondre à ces différents besoins, dans le cadre de l’actualisation de la loi française de programmation militaire.
Selon le  communiqué de KNDS du 20 novembre , le site de La Chapelle-Saint-Ursin compte environ 500 salariés et recrute actuellement plus de 150 profils qualifiés, notamment dans la production et l’ingénierie système.

Le Royaume-Uni conduit des opérations cyber offensives contre la Russie, la Chine, l’Iran et la Corée du Nord. Le général Sir Rob Magowan, commandant du Cyber & Specialist Operations Command, l’a confirmé dans un entretien publié vendredi 20 novembre 2026 par  Sky News , en désignant ces quatre pays comme des adversaires actifs dans le cyberespace.
Interrogé sur l’activité de la National Cyber Force, chargée des opérations informatiques offensives, le responsable militaire a répondu par l’affirmative. Il a également cité la criminalité organisée parmi les cibles de cette unité britannique, dont les missions opérationnelles restent largement secrètes.
Rob Magowan a expliqué que Londres cherchait à imposer un coût aux acteurs qui s’attaquent aux systèmes britanniques. Il a écarté l’expression de guerre ouverte et décrit une confrontation menée sous le seuil d’un conflit militaire déclaré.
Créée en 2020, la National Cyber Force associe le GCHQ, le ministère de la Défense, le MI6 et le Defence Science and Technology Laboratory. Elle intervient contre les menaces émanant d’États et de réseaux criminels ou terroristes, en appui aux capacités de défense et de renseignement du Royaume-Uni.
Le 16 novembre, le roi Charles III a inauguré le nouveau siège de la force, Ribble House, à Samlesbury, dans le Lancashire. Le  communiqué du gouvernement britannique  présente cette installation comme un renforcement des moyens de l’unité, dont les personnels proviennent de plusieurs services de sécurité nationale.
Dans son  bilan annuel 2026 , le National Cyber Security Centre fait état de 1 831 signalements de cyberattaques entre septembre 2025 et août 2026. Sur ces signalements, 337 incidents ont nécessité une intervention de ses équipes, dont 80 classés d’importance nationale.

original_payload.original_title: Caifadine Manasse garante continuidade do apoio do Governo ao desporto moçambicano
original_payload.original_body:
O ministro da Juventude e Desporto, Caifadine Manasse, reafirmou o compromisso do Governo em continuar a apoiar e valorizar o desporto moçambicano, destacando o papel do futebol nacional na afirmação dos atletas e das equipas do país no panorama desportivo internacional.
Falando durante as celebrações da Black Bulls, no encerramento do Moçambola, o governante considerou que a edição deste ano da principal prova do futebol nacional foi marcada por desafios, mas conseguiu chegar ao fim com resultados positivos e num ambiente de festa.
“Como Governo, o que vamos continuar a fazer é acarinharmos este desporto moçambicano, que cada vez mais mostra que os moçambicanos estão à altura do desporto mundial”, afirmou Caifadine Manasse.
O ministro destacou ainda a importância de continuar a mobilizar esforços para garantir o crescimento e a valorização do futebol nacional, defendendo que o Moçambola deve continuar a ser uma competição capaz de começar e terminar em ambiente de celebração.
Apesar dos constrangimentos registados ao longo da competição, Manasse considerou positivo o facto de o campeonato ter sido concluído, sublinhando a necessidade de o Governo continuar a dar o seu contributo para o desenvolvimento do desporto.
Relativamente ao apoio às equipas, o governante explicou que a relação entre o Governo e os clubes passa também pelas estruturas organizativas do futebol, nomeadamente a Liga Moçambicana de Futebol e a Federação Moçambicana de Futebol.
Segundo Caifadine Manasse, a presença do Governo nas celebrações da Black Bulls demonstra o seu envolvimento e a interação com os diferentes intervenientes do futebol nacional.
“O Governo está presente em todos os acontecimentos do futebol moçambicano”, assegurou o ministro, reiterando a disposição do Executivo em continuar a acompanhar e acarinhá-lo.

items.title: PR lança primeira pedra para construção do edifício parlamentar em Mocuba

original_payload.original_title: PR lança primeira pedra para construção do edifício parlamentar em Mocuba
original_payload.original_body:
Daniel Chapo lança a primeira pedra para a construção do edifício da Assembleia da República, orçado em mais de 150 milhões de dólares. O empreendimento integra um projecto de 6.400 hectares e deverá estar concluído até 2029.
Mocuba, na província da Zambézia, prepara-se para acolher uma nova centralidade político-institucional do país. O Presidente da República, Daniel Chapo, lançou, este sábado, a primeira pedra para a construção do edifício da Assembleia da República, um empreendimento orçado em mais de 150 milhões de dólares, com conclusão prevista para 2029. O projecto obedecerá a duas fases: a primeira consiste na construção do edifício parlamentar e a segunda na implantação da cidadela parlamentar.
A infra-estrutura constitui a primeira fase da implantação da futura cidadela parlamentar, projectada para uma área de aproximadamente 6.400 hectares. O complexo deverá integrar, além do edifício da Assembleia da República, um complexo residencial parlamentar, gabinetes de trabalho, o Instituto Nacional de Estudos Parlamentares e outras infra-estruturas de apoio.
A iniciativa representa a materialização de uma promessa feita por Daniel Chapo durante a campanha eleitoral de 2024 e enquadra-se na visão do Governo de descentralização das instituições do Estado.
No âmbito da preparação do espaço para a implantação do projecto, 25 hectares, anteriormente ocupados por residências, já foram disponibilizados. Segundo as informações apresentadas durante a cerimónia, 35 famílias foram reassentadas, após um processo de compensação.
Na ocasião, o governador da Zambézia, Pio Matos, destacou a importância estratégica de Mocuba para o desenvolvimento económico da província e do país, considerando que a implantação da cidadela parlamentar poderá reforçar a posição do distrito como centro de convergência de diferentes dinâmicas de desenvolvimento.
“A iniciativa de transformar algumas províncias em capitais temáticas, atribuindo a cada uma um papel específico na estrutura funcional e simbólica do Estado moçambicano, representa uma nova abordagem na organização e governação do país. Esta visão procura promover uma distribuição mais equilibrada das funções do Estado e impulsionar o desenvolvimento integrado de todas as regiões de Moçambique”, disse o governador da Zambézia.
Por sua vez, a presidente da Assembleia da República, Margarida Talapa, classificou o momento como histórico, por representar a expansão da presença do Poder Legislativo para além da capital do país.
“Em nome do povo que representamos, expressamos a nossa profunda gratidão a Vossa Excelência, Senhor Presidente da República, por honrar a palavra dada e tornar realidade o compromisso de trazer o Poder Legislativo à cidade de Mocuba. Que esta obra seja mais do que um edifício. Que se transforme num símbolo de aproximação entre regiões, de união entre cidadãos e de convergência entre diferentes formas de pensar, sempre ao serviço de uma causa maior: Moçambique e o seu povo”, disse a presidente da Assembleia da República.
Já o Presidente da República considerou que o lançamento da primeira pedra constitui um marco importante para a democracia moçambicana. Daniel Chapo convidou os quatro chefes das bancadas parlamentares a saudarem os presentes, num gesto que simbolizou a união da Casa do Povo.
O Chefe do Estado rejeitou a interpretação de que o empreendimento seja um mero expediente eleitoral, defendendo que a iniciativa está associada à visão de renovação de Moçambique, assente na paz, na prosperidade e na melhoria das condições de vida dos cidadãos.
“A construção deste edifício enquadra-se na visão de renovação de Moçambique e na construção de um novo pacto com o povo. A edificação de uma nova Assembleia Parlamentar, moderna e construída de raiz, reafirma o compromisso do Governo da República de Moçambique em trabalhar em articulação com os demais órgãos do Estado, tendo como referência o princípio constitucional da separação e interdependência dos poderes dos órgãos de soberania.

items.title: Black Bulls conquista terceiro título, apesar da derrota

original_payload.original_title: Black Bulls conquista terceiro título, apesar da derrota
original_payload.original_body:
A Associação Black Bulls recebeu, ontem, o troféu de campeão nacional do Moçambola 2026, apesar da derrota por três bolas sem resposta diante do Ferroviário de Maputo, na última jornada da prova. Os Touros terminaram o campeonato na liderança, com 56 pontos, em 26 jornadas, conquistando o título pela terceira vez na sua história.
A festa do título começou com um duelo entre os campeões e o Ferroviário de Maputo, que se deslocou a Tchumene determinado a conquistar os três pontos, apesar de já não ter possibilidades de terminar a prova entre os primeiros classificados.
Com as bancadas preenchidas, os Locomotivas da capital dominaram o marcador e venceram por três bolas sem resposta. Clésio Baúque, aos 35 minutos, Celso Calisto, aos 48, e Max, aos 84 minutos, marcaram os golos que ditaram a derrota dos anfitriões.
O resultado, contudo, não alterou a classificação final, com a Black Bulls a terminar no primeiro lugar, somando 56 pontos, ao cabo de 26 jornadas, garantindo o terceiro título nacional.
No balanço da temporada, o treinador da Black Bulls, Nelson Santos, e o seu homólogo do Ferroviário de Maputo fizeram a avaliação da prestação das respectivas equipas.
Por sua vez, Juneid Lalgy, patrono e proprietário do projecto Black Bulls, considerou que a época foi atípica e exigiu sacrifícios adicionais para que a equipa alcançasse o objectivo de conquistar o campeonato.
Já o presidente da Liga Moçambicana de Futebol, Alberto Simango Júnior, reconheceu os desafios enfrentados ao longo da temporada, considerando que a competição decorreu dentro das condições existentes, ao mesmo tempo que perspectiva melhorias para a próxima edição.
Com a conquista do Moçambola 2026, a Black Bulls assegura a representação de Moçambique nas competições africanas de clubes, onde terá pela frente o desafio de lutar pelo acesso à Liga dos Campeões Africanos.

items.title: South Africa: Former Deputy President Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka Dies

original_payload.original_title: South Africa: Former Deputy President Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka Dies
original_payload.original_body:
Cape Town — Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka, South Africa's first woman deputy president and a former United Nations under-secretary-general, has died at 71, the South African government  announced  on Friday.
Acting President Paul Mashatile conveyed condolences on behalf of President Cyril Ramaphosa, who is in the U.S., and said further details would be shared in consultation with the family.
A former anti-apartheid activist and member of parliament (MP), Mlambo-Ngcuka was deputy president from 2005 to 2008. She also served as minister of minerals and energy and as deputy minister of trade and industry.
She was in the first generation of MPs in South Africa's democratic Parliament, and sat in the Constitutional Assembly, which helped draft the country's democratic Constitution. Her time as deputy president was under President Thabo Mbeki.

items.title: Africa: WGS Dialogue for Latin America and the Caribbean Explores Stronger Cooperation in Shaping the Future

original_payload.original_title: Africa: WGS Dialogue for Latin America and the Caribbean Explores Stronger Cooperation in Shaping the Future
original_payload.original_body:
10   heads of state and government and international organisations
His Excellency Luis Abinader, President of the Dominican Republic, expressed his country's appreciation for the commitment of His Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, President of the UAE, and His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President and Prime Minister of the UAE and Ruler of Dubai, to investing in a long-term strategic relationship with the Dominican Republic. He reaffirmed his country's commitment to strengthening these relations and taking them to new heights.
He noted that hosting the World Governments Summit Dialogue for Latin America and the Caribbean reflects the two countries' shared vision and commitment to providing a platform that brings together governments, business leaders, international organisations and experts to open a new chapter in relations and intensify joint efforts to shape the future.
The President of the Dominican Republic said: "His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum put forward an idea that deserves to guide this Dialogue: what is the 'currency' of the future? Is it water? Artificial intelligence? Energy? His Highness offered an answer that carries a profound lesson: trust is the currency of the future."
His remarks came at the opening of the World Governments Summit Dialogue for Latin America and the Caribbean, held in Cap Cana, Dominican Republic, with the participation of 10 leaders of states, governments, and regional and international organisations, more than 70 speakers, representatives of over 30 countries, and 120 private-sector companies. Participants exchanged perspectives on the future of partnerships and international cooperation across 35 dialogue sessions and 15 leadership meetings. The programme covered six themes: geoeconomics and strategic investment; tourism, culture and experience economies; international cooperation and regional integration; foresight for the future of governments; logistics and global connectivity; and human capital and the future of work.
His Excellency Luis Abinader said: "We gather today with a shared conviction that the future is shaped by the decisions we make and the relationships we sustain. Last year, when we hosted this Dialogue, we affirmed the Dominican Republic's readiness to serve as a trusted bridge connecting Latin America and the Caribbean with the Middle East."
He added: "The Dominican Republic is committed to this initiative because it has succeeded in consolidating political, social and economic stability, and seeks to turn these achievements into new opportunities for its people. We also believe in dialogue as a means of strengthening relations and deepening connections. We look forward to building on these strengths to forge closer partnerships with the UAE, supported by a committed government, a private sector ready to invest, and organisations capable of sustaining and deepening dialogue and translating it into tangible results."
He explained that his country sees the future of relations between Latin America and the Caribbean and the Middle East in broader cooperation between businesses, stronger investment flows, knowledge exchange and deeper ties between communities. He noted that the UAE's experience demonstrates what can be achieved through long-term vision and hard work, stressing that its expertise in logistics, connectivity, tourism and innovation offers significant opportunities for cooperation.
His Excellency Luis Abinader said: "The importance of the World Governments Summit lies in its ability to bring together people who can learn from one another and work together. One government's experience can help improve services in another country. The Dominican Republic invests in this platform because it believes in the strength of these connections and is committed to this partnership for the long term."
Mohammed Al Gergawi: UAE leadership embraces a comprehensive vision for international cooperation
His Excellency Mohammad Abdullah Al Gergawi, Minister of Cabinet Affairs and Chairman of the World Governments Summit, affirmed that, under the guidance of its wise leadership, the UAE embraces a comprehensive vision for international cooperation, based on partnerships to shape the future, improve quality of life and ensure a better tomorrow for future generations.

About the dialogue
The African Development Bank Group invites you to a high-level dialogue on ending gender-based violence in Africa, as part of the 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence campaign, a global movement to raise awareness, mobilize advocacy and drive action to prevent and eliminate violence against women and girls worldwide.
Why this dialogue matters
Gender-based violence affects the safety, health and livelihoods of millions of women and girls across Africa. It also limits their ability to learn, work, participate in the economy and contribute to their communities. The consequences extend beyond individual survivors, affecting families, institutions and the continent's economic future.
Ending this violence requires more than commitment. It requires sustained investment in approaches that prevent violence, protect survivors, strengthen access to justice and hold perpetrators accountable.
Development finance institutions have an important role to play, including through the projects they finance, the safeguards they put in place and their support for stronger national systems.

items.title: Liberia: Diaspora Voting Campaign Gains Momentum As 2029 Elections Approach

original_payload.original_title: Liberia: Diaspora Voting Campaign Gains Momentum As 2029 Elections Approach
original_payload.original_body:
A growing campaign to allow Liberians living abroad to vote in national elections is gaining momentum, with diaspora advocates and lawmakers pressing for legislation and an operational framework ahead of the 2029 elections.
At the center of the renewed effort is the All-Liberia Conference on Dual Citizenship (ALCOD), which will host its 2026 Liberian Overseas Voting Rights Summit on November 21 at The Ohio State University in Columbus, Ohio, under the theme, "Paving the Way for Out-of-Country Voting."
Sponsored by the university's Center for African Studies and ALCOD, the summit will bring together diaspora leaders, lawmakers, academics and election stakeholders to examine how eligible Liberians abroad could participate in national elections without travelling home.

The Meles Zenawi era brought a long-awaited sense of relief and ecstasy to the people of Tigray after years of struggle, suffering, and uncertainty. This shift from prolonged agony to renewed hope was captured in the title of the late Dr. Solomon Enkuay's book,   The Agony and Ecstasy of Tigray  --a title that evokes historical contradictions: the enduring pain of oppression and conflict, alongside the exhilaration of hard-won political transformation and a new social contract.

items.title: Africa: UNAIDS Mourns Dr Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka, Former Executive Director of UN Women and Champion of the HIV Response

original_payload.original_title: Africa: UNAIDS Mourns Dr Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka, Former Executive Director of UN Women and Champion of the HIV Response
original_payload.original_body:
Geneva/Pretoria — UNAIDS is deeply saddened by the passing of Dr Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka, former United Nations Under-Secretary-General and Executive Director of UN Women, and South Africa's first woman Deputy President, who has died at the age of 71.
From 2013 to 2021, as Executive Director of UN Women, Dr Mlambo-Ngcuka served on the UNAIDS Committee of Cosponsoring Organizations. In that role she was a steadfast partner to the Joint Programme and a powerful voice for placing the rights, leadership and safety of women and girls at the centre of the global HIV response.
Her commitment to the HIV response was rooted at home. As Deputy President of South Africa, she chaired the South African National AIDS Council (SANAC) at a defining moment in the country's response. In 2007 she led the launch of a restructured SANAC, which brought government, civil society, business and labour together as partners and endorsed the National Strategic Plan for HIV, AIDS and STIs 2007-2011. She worked effortlessly to build trust and strong partnerships between government and civil society, including people living with HIV, and insisted that the response be owned by all South Africans. She also called for the HIV response to be linked to the 16 Days of Activism for No Violence Against Women and Children. UNAIDS was proud to work alongside SANAC and the Department of Health in that process.

Au Niger, la croissance démographique et les aléas climatiques contribuent depuis plusieurs années à la réduction des terres cultivables. Près des trois quarts du territoire national sont constitués de zones arides ou désertiques.
Face à cette situation, la récupération des terres dégradées constitue un enjeu majeur pour les populations rurales, dont les activités dépendent en grande partie de l’agriculture.
Mais une fois ces terres restaurées, comment assurer leur gestion et leur exploitation durable ? Quelles solutions permettent de les préserver tout en contribuant à l’alimentation des familles ?
Autant de questions abordées dans ce magazine.

items.title: Kenya: découverte de plusieurs cadavres d’hippopotames victimes des activités humaines

original_payload.original_title: Kenya: découverte de plusieurs cadavres d’hippopotames victimes des activités humaines
original_payload.original_body:
Kenya: découverte de plusieurs cadavres d’hippopotames victimes des activités humaines
Au Kenya, c’est l’inquiétude après la découverte de plusieurs cadavres d’hippopotames. Depuis quinze jours, une douzaine de ces animaux sauvages ont été retrouvés morts, sur les rives du lac Naivasha, au nord-ouest de Nairobi. Les Services kényans de la faune (KWS) ont lancé une enquête et les premières autopsies révèlent que les animaux sont victimes des activités humaines.
Publié le :  21/11/2026 - 16:27
1 min     Temps de lecture
Un hippopotame est assis, partiellement immergé dans les eaux d’une inondation, tandis qu’un martin-pêcheur survole les lieux. La montée des eaux du lac Naivasha a submergé des zones boisées situées sur ses rives, ainsi que des bâtiments et des infrastructures dans la ville de Naivasha, située au bord du lac, dans la vallée du Rift au Kenya, le 3 octobre 2020        AFP - TONY KARUMBA
Par :
RFI
Publicité
Avec notre correspondante à Nairobi,   Gaëlle Laleix
Dans un communiqué, KWS révèle les résultats des deux premières autopsies réalisées. Un filet de pêche a été retrouvé au fond de l’estomac du premier hippopotame, provoquant sa mort par suffocation. Le second serait décédé après avoir ingéré une quantité importante de tiges de maïs, provoquant une accumulation de gaz dans son estomac.
D’après l’Unité de gestion de la plage de Kamere et l’Organisation des pêcheurs du lac Naivasha – deux associations locales –, les dépouilles d’autres hippopotames présentaient un estomac anormalement gonflé. Certains animaux agonisants paraissaient souffrir de difficultés respiratoires.
Conflits entre la faune et les hommes de plus en plus récurrents
Grace Nyambura, présidente de l’Organisation des pêcheurs, estime qu’il s’agit là de la plus grave série de morts d’hippopotames depuis des années.
Les conflits entre la faune et les hommes sont de plus en plus récurrents à Naivasha. La montée des eaux du lac et l’extension de l’agriculture poussent les hippopotames à se rapprocher des lieux d’activité humaine.
Par ailleurs, les pêcheurs illégaux, à pied, sont de plus en plus nombreux et s’exposent aux attaques de ces animaux gigantesques. Selon les organisations locales, plus de 20 personnes sont mortes tuées par des hippopotames à Naivasha, depuis le début de l’année.
À lire aussi  Kenya: un potentiel empoisonnement à l'origine de la mort de 15 éléphants

General News  Sokoto varsity Alumni hold Health Walk, donate N500,000 to hospital
By  Ismail Abdulaziz   ·   3 hours ago   ·  1 min read
✓
✓
The Usmanu Danfodiyo University Sokoto (UDUS) Alumni Association, FCT Chapter, on Saturday held a fitness walk in Abuja and donated N500,000 to indigent patients at Maitama District Hospital.
The event started around Unity Fountain, near Millennium Park, with an aerobic warm-up for a large turnout of alumni, followed by a walk to Maitama Roundabout and back.
FCT Chapter Secretary-General, Gimba Abdul, said the walk doubled as a reunion to reconnect former colleagues, celebrate friendship and brotherhood, and network for mutual progress.
‘’It was not just a walk. It was a reunion. It was a celebration of friendship, fitness, and brotherhood,’’ Abdul said.
Representatives of UDUS, Umar Jabo, and the National Alumni body, Bashir Muhammed, joined chapter executives and members at the event.
After the walk, a delegation visited Maitama District Hospital to provide N500,000 in cash assistance for indigent patients, while attendees received Smart Cups and Ceramic Cups as souvenirs.
Abdul thanked Almighty Allah and commended executives, university and national representatives, members, and contributors for the successful outing. (NAN)
