items.title: MDN reforça controlo e protecção da informação Classificada

original_payload.original_title: MDN reforça controlo e protecção da informação Classificada
original_payload.original_body:
O Ministério da Defesa Nacional (MDN) está a reforçar os mecanismos de controlo, tratamento e protecção da informação classificada nos órgãos do sector da Defesa, através do II Seminário Metodológico para Chefes das Secretarias de Informação Classificada do MDN e das Forças Armadas de Defesa de Moçambique (FADM), iniciado esta quinta-feira, 19 de Novembro, em Maputo.
A iniciativa visa dotar os responsáveis destas unidades de conhecimentos e ferramentas para prevenir o extravio, a divulgação não autorizada e o uso indevido de documentos e matérias classificadas, bem como uniformizar os procedimentos de gestão da informação nas instituições do sector.
Na abertura do encontro, o Secretário Permanente do MDN, Casimiro Augusto Mueio, instou os participantes a reforçarem o rigor e a disciplina no exercício das suas funções, advertindo que a protecção do Segredo do Estado constitui uma responsabilidade institucional e um imperativo para a defesa da soberania nacional.
Ao longo de dois dias, os participantes vão trabalhar matérias relacionadas com o tratamento de informação classificada, segurança informática, sigilo profissional, organização das Secretarias de Informação Classificada, classificação documental e implementação do Sistema Nacional de Arquivos do Estado (SNAE).
Mueio advertiu ainda que a violação das normas relativas ao Segredo do Estado constitui ilícito criminal, apelando ao cumprimento rigoroso dos procedimentos legais e técnicos para evitar falhas que possam comprometer a segurança da informação e o funcionamento das instituições.

items.title: NPM Presidential candidate supports NEC’s postponement of elections

original_payload.original_title: NPM Presidential candidate supports NEC’s postponement of elections
original_payload.original_body:
The presidential candidate of the National Patriotic Movement (NPM), Issa Muzamil Sebit Makelele, on Sunday said he supports the move by the National Elections Commission (NEC) to defer the general elections initially scheduled for 22 December to 11 February 2027.
He made the remarks while registering as a voter in Juba’s Malakia suburb and said the postponement allows parties more time to campaign.
“My party supports the decision of the NEC as the postponement of the election date gives political parties the necessary time to complete their political campaigns,” he said. “My election campaigns will move to the states of Western Equatoria, Eastern Equatoria, and Western Bahr el Ghazal, after the conclusion of the campaigns in Central Equatoria State.”
Addressing the press after registering, Muzamil urged eligible voters to register and embrace the election process and choose their leaders.
“I came to my name today (Sunday) as a voter in this country,” he said. “This country has never had elections since independence, so let us participate in this historic moment for South Sudan.”

items.title: Opinion| Guarantors should push for peace implementation instead of elections in South Sudan

original_payload.original_title: Opinion| Guarantors should push for peace implementation instead of elections in South Sudan
original_payload.original_body:
The primary purpose of this article is to convey my opinion to South Sudan’s 2018 peace guarantors, including the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD), the African Union (AU), the United Nations (UN), and the Troika (the United States, the United Kingdom, and Norway), to stop South Sudan’s government from proceeding with general elections and revert to the implementation of the 2018 peace agreement.
Elections were designed to be the culmination of a structured political transition, not a shortcut around it. Key prerequisites stipulated in the R-ARCSS remain dangerously unfulfilled. In this article, I highlight some critical challenges that disqualify the SPLM-IG from conducting unilateral general elections without the participation of the SPLM/A-IO, SSOA, FDs, and OPP. The non-signatory parties President Salva Kiir has mobilized to ‘challenge’ him in the sham elections are just rubber stamps and insignificant. They provide a facade of multiparty democracy while lacking independent constituencies and just want to validate the elections and give Kiir legitimacy as an elected president.
South Sudan’s one-party-handpicked so-called “National Election Commission” announced the postponement of the single-party elections from December 2026 to February 2027. The delay comes as a result of the electoral commission’s desire for more time to distribute registration materials and conduct civic education. Those activities will be carried out amid growing violence and political tensions across the country. They want to conduct a unilateral election to legitimize Kiir.
If South Sudan continues to be led by Kiir, the country’s political stability and desirable economic development will only deteriorate. Furthermore, ethnic divisions, corruption, and underfunded public services will destabilize social stability. South Sudan stands at a dangerous crossroads at the moment. Moving forward with general elections before fulfilling the foundational pillars of the 2018 revitalized peace agreement threatens to plunge the country back into full-scale civil war. As international guarantors, you must intervene decisively to halt these premature polls and compel the government in Juba to return to genuine implementation of the agreement.
In short, the political atmosphere in the Republic of South Sudan is characterized by deep polarization, widespread public frustration, and a sharp rejection of incumbent President Kiir’s leadership following the outbreak of the civil war in 2013, 2016, and 2025. Kiir’s recent political and electoral moves undermine the implementation of the core 2018 Revitalized Peace Agreement. His refusal to implement peace prerequisites made the conduct of the election flawed and undesirable. The elections are meant to bring South Sudan’s post-conflict transition to an end.
South Sudan’s general elections, now rescheduled for February 2027, need to be postponed given that they are not inclusive. The country should be focused on repairing the broken 2018 peace agreement that Kiir abrogated and doesn’t want to implement entirely. The government has opted to pursue a path of selective implementation of the 2018 peace agreement and systematically sidelining other political parties from participating. Without the participation of the other political parties, urgent political consensus and adherence to the Revitalized Peace Agreement on the Resolution of the Conflict in the Republic of South Sudan (R-ARCSS), the elections will face a credibility crisis. At the moment, the only immediate need is to find a necessary political framework that can move the country towards a legitimate democratic process rather than conducting an election that will result in ethnic domination and endless civil war.
The signatories to the Revitalized Peace Agreement must be reminded that South Sudan is facing severe political tensions, shrinking civic space, and heightened conflict as it approaches national elections. They need to stop the government from proceeding with elections. Other actors like Reconstituted Joint Monitoring and Evaluation Commission (RJMEC) that were established to oversee unresolved political disputes and incomplete security reforms, should also be involved in stopping the government from continuing with the election. The growing uncertainty surrounding the general election stems from the weak implementation of the R-ARCSS, which set clear guidelines to be followed before any general elections can take place. Failure to do so will increase the danger as fighting continues in many parts of the country, and the rule of law and justice mechanisms envisioned by R-ARCSS remain incomplete. Moreover, the arrest and the trial of former Vice President Dr. Riek Machar, who is also the leader of the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-in-Opposition (SPLM-IO), is a serious concern as the government intentionally keeps him away from participating in the election.
The 2018 Revitalized Peace Agreement did not envision general elections as a stand-alone event, as Salva Kiir and his party project. The peace agreement projects an election for every party. Elections were meant to be the last phase of the transitional process, setting the foundation for post-conflict reconstruction in South Sudan. The R-ARCSS sought, among many things, to establish a unified security force, a permanent constitution, a functioning electoral system, and a transitional justice system. As such, the general elections cannot be separated from the R-ARCSS. The implementation of the R-ARCSS has been very slow, and the parties adopted a roadmap that extended the transitional period and moved the general elections to December 2026 because many critical tasks had remained unresolved. The parties justified each extension as additional time needed to complete reforms that will enable a credible transition.
The debate changed in September 2026 when the electoral framework was amended to remove the completion of the permanent constitution and national census as prerequisites for conducting national elections. This may remove legal and practical obstacles to conducting the election, but it also changes the sequencing envisioned by the peace agreement. The reconfiguration of the institutions through which the R-ARCSS power-sharing agreement had been operated has significantly changed the political context. Just a week before the dissolution, the regional body IGAD reaffirmed R-ARCSS as the “sole viable framework for peace,” and the December election remained anchored to the peace agreement. The question now is how the institutions established to monitor and implement the agreement will operate under the caretaker administration.
The Kiir government bypassed some unfinished reforms, such as security-sector unification, electoral rules, the political rights of parties, civic space, and dispute resolution. Transitional justice remains incomplete because the Hybrid Court and the Compensation and Reparation Authority, which were supposed to be established, are still pending, even as the Commission for Truth, Reconciliation and Healing is still pending. Many of the clauses of the Revitalized Peace Agreement have not been implemented. This was supposed to be the basis for any general elections.
Political actors in South Sudan, particularly Kiir and his cronies, are not concerned that every aspect of the R-ARCSS has not been implemented before the general elections can take place. That stance made other actors wonder, asking for clarity and full implementation of the peace agreement before a free, fair, and peaceful election could be conducted. When R-ARCSS was designed, the general elections were supposed to be the outcome of the transition. However, under current circumstances, the risk is that holding general elections becomes a substitute for completing the transition without implementing all provisions. This concern has become immediate because of the dissolution of the transitional government. The critical question now is whether the new caretaker administration can oversee the elections in a way that all political parties and actors regard as sufficiently inclusive and legitimate.
Well-wishers and many South Sudanese citizens who are watching from distant shores are concerned that the government wants to conduct elections without first conducting a census. They can only imagine that the move of bypassing a census count will make it harder to know the number of voters. Voter registration will determine who is eligible to vote, but the absence of a new census complicates demographic and constituency questions.
The September amendments have now settled the legal question of whether the election can proceed without a new census, but they do not resolve the practical challenge lying ahead. The immediate challenge for the National Election Commission is whether it can complete a credible voter registration across all states, conduct civic education that clearly explains the rules, and finance the operation transparently and predictably. Salva Kiir has intentionally delinked requirements linking general elections with a permanent constitution and a national census.
In October, the SPLM Party commenced the process leading up to primary elections. Other political parties have not done the same. If implemented correctly, the agreement would recognize SPLM-IG, led by President Kiir, SPLM/A-IO, led by Dr. Riek Machar, SSOA, Former Detainees (FD), and Other Political Parties (OPP) to contest equally and launch their primary elections simultaneously. A unilateral election process without consensus and participation of all parties to the 2018 peace agreement is a recipe for returning the country to full-scale violence. The best thing Salva Kiir can do now is the immediate and unconditional release of Dr. Riek Machar and other political detainees.
Kiir does not want to compete with anybody. He is using political hooliganism, which is perhaps the most abysmal manifestation of democratic schizophrenia. If your political party cannot tolerate another political party campaigning within the same geographical territory, then what precisely are you campaigning for?
Democracy is fundamentally about the freedom to mobilize, canvass, persuade, debate, and intellectually engage the electorate. Yet, with bewildering suddenness, political antagonism degenerates into intimidation, disruption, and confrontation. Has democratic campaigning now metamorphosed into some barbaric gladiatorial coliseum where political disagreement must inevitably culminate in confrontation? Do you find political propositions intellectually disagreeable? Magnificent! Present your candidate. Brandish your manifesto. Unleash your statistics. Deploy your intellectual artillery. Defeat the argument with a superior argument.
To deliberately disrupt another party’s peaceful political mobilization merely because its presence threatens your political calculations is nothing short of democratic atavism, a primitive regression into political domination through intimidation and coercion. Democracy does not operate by the jurisprudence of frustration, where the inability to intellectually vanquish an opponent becomes justification for obstructing his microphone. If another political organization is exercising its democratic right to campaign, it could be permitted to campaign.
What are some indications, illustrated, that Salva Kiir is working on abdicating power and relinquishing it to one of his children or fellow tribesmen? There have been indications that South Sudanese political observers and analysts deem tactical appointments to consolidate power within his family or a potential successor among his tribesmen. For example, in early 2025, President Kiir appointed Benjamin Bol Mel as Vice President and first deputy chairman of the ruling SPLM Party. The move brought widespread speculation that he was being groomed as Kiir’s successor. However, President Kiir abruptly dismissed Bol Mel on November 12, 2025, stripping him of his vice presidency, removing him from the ruling SPLM party leadership, and demoting him within the National Security Service. No official successor has been named to replace him in that capacity, and James Wani Igga was subsequently reappointed to the vice president position.
At the same time, President Salva Kiir appointed his daughter, Adut Salva Kiir, as Senior Presidential Envoy for Special Programs. A position previously held by Benjamin Bol Mel, before he was elevated to the vice president position. The move was criticized as a clear nepotism political dynasty within the country’s leadership. In September 2026, Salva Kiir appointed his son, Major General Atem Salva Kiir, as commander of the presidential guard. The appointment has again attracted the attention of South Sudanese political observers and analysts that Salva Kiir is preparing his children to succeed him in the foreseeable future. Kiir, who is 74, has been in power since South Sudan gained independence in 2011 and has not said when he is going to retire from politics.
Kiir remains in power and continues to issue major political decrees. He seems to be incapacitated. Whenever he is travelling abroad for diplomatic engagements, South Sudanese people are worried, wondering whether he will represent the country with dignity and clarity. Unfortunately, many of these appearances have raised serious concerns about his ability to think and speak coherently. His physical and cognitive decline has fueled intense speculation about who is actually drafting and executing President Kiir’s sweeping decrees. Political analysts note that decrees are formulated behind closed doors with minimal transparency, relying heavily on a tight circle of loyalists, military intelligence figures, and traditional advisors like the Jieng Council of Elders. Additionally, internal discussions within the presidency have reportedly focused on succession and elevating family members, including his daughter or his son, which will make South Sudan a nepotistic dynasty.
In conclusion, South Sudan’s general elections, previously scheduled to be conducted in December, now pushed to 11 February 2027, need to be stopped by the 2018 peace guarantors. The 2018 peace agreement established safe, free, fair, peaceful, inclusive, and transparent elections, not unilateral abrogation of the agreement. If peace guarantors allow President Kiir to proceed with the elections, the result will be an implementation of nepotism or single tribe ethnocracy.
International actors should push for a consensual extension with a clear, time-bound roadmap to elections. This could salvage the deal and save the country from returning to entrenched large-scale violence. It would also save the country from being a family nepotocracy or a single tribe ethnocracy. We in the SPLM-IO are yearning for a faithful implementation of all provisions enshrined in the peace agreement. Achieving faithful implementation would start by reverting to talks that would be conducted under regional and international mediation, which must include IGAD, the African Union, the Troika, and the United Nations, among other peace-loving international organizations.
Respectively.
The writer is a political commentator and the author of the book “South Sudan’s Endless Sorrows.” He can be reached via  lulgatluak09@gmail.com .

items.title: Damazin transport fares soar as security fears persist

original_payload.original_title: Damazin transport fares soar as security fears persist
original_payload.original_body:
Transport fares from Damazin, the capital of Sudan’s Blue Nile Region, have surged amid a growing shortage of transport services and an increasing number of residents seeking to leave the city, as recent military clashes and security concerns continue to fuel public anxiety and uncertainty.
The mounting concerns come amid continued fighting between the SAF and allied forces on one side, and the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement (SPLM), operating under the Tasis Alliance, on the other.
During a visit to Damazin’s Al-Shaabi Market, Radio Tamazuj found that long-distance bus fares to Khartoum ranged between 180,000 and 220,000 Sudanese pounds (SDG), while fares for private intercity taxis stood at approximately SDG 400,000 per passenger. Hiring an entire taxi costs as much as SDG 4 million.
Several residents reported a sharp increase in transport fares over the past few days, compounded by a decline in the availability of vehicles. The situation has resulted in overcrowding at transport terminals and mounting difficulties in securing tickets, particularly for families seeking to leave the city.
Rami Kamal, a resident of Damazin, said a bus ticket to Khartoum cost approximately SDG 180,000, while intercity taxi fares ranged between SDG 300,000 and SDG 400,000 per passenger.
“Despite the steep fares, others and I have been unable to secure tickets and are uncertain about what to do next,” he stated.
Meanwhile, the Government of Blue Nile State continues to issue messages of reassurance, urging residents not to be swayed by rumors and maintaining that the security situation across the region remains stable.
Saif Al-Nasr Minallah, the state government spokesperson, said the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and allied forces were encircling opposing forces, who he claimed were retreating along several fronts.
“Advances by government forces are expanding areas of relative safety and reducing the threat of violence and intimidation,” he said. “Normal life is returning to Damazin.”
The spokesperson urged residents to go about their daily lives as usual, including attending schools and visiting shops and markets.
Amid growing concerns over security developments and the soaring cost of leaving Damazin, many residents face an increasingly difficult choice: remain in the city until the situation becomes clearer or leave despite financial constraints and the scarcity of transport.
Tariq Al-Tayyib, another resident, said thousands of families found themselves in an increasingly desperate predicament, unable to decide whether to stay or leave.
“Mounting security fears have made remaining in the city increasingly difficult, while prohibitive transport costs have left many families unable to afford to leave,” he said. “The rising prices and the escalating cost of travel have effectively trapped many families in Damazin, with those who could afford the fares managing to leave while those without sufficient financial means remained stranded in the city.”
He added that residents were grappling with uncertainty over whether to leave, particularly amid concerns about the safety of travel routes.
He questioned where residents could seek refuge when they appeared to have little choice but to remain in the city.
Al-Tayyib appealed to the relevant authorities to provide residents with clear assurances about the security situation and their safety amid the unfolding developments.
Hostilities continue across several parts of the Blue Nile Region, including Kurmuk, Geissan, Bau, and Wad Al-Mahi localities, amid reports that fighting is drawing closer to populated areas, including residential settlements 10, 11, and 12, as well as Dering and Maganza.

items.title: Feature| Poverty and exploitation jeopardize Juba schoolgirls’ dreams

original_payload.original_title: Feature| Poverty and exploitation jeopardize Juba schoolgirls’ dreams
original_payload.original_body:
At 19, Nancy Modo dreams of becoming a pediatrician to save the lives of South Sudanese children. However, after completing Senior Four at New Apostolic Secondary School in Juba, she faces an uncertain future as financial hardship threatens to prevent her from continuing her education.
Rising living costs in Juba, school fees, expensive transport, and a lack of necessities are among the challenges Nancy says girls face as they struggle to stay in school and pursue their ambitions.
“My biggest challenge, first of all, is lack of school fees to continue with my university process,” Nancy told Radio Tamazuj. “And second is money for transport. With the crises in Juba, things are becoming more expensive and very hard. And managing transport is so hard.”
She says the financial burden extends beyond paying school fees. Girls who cannot afford transport may have to walk long distances to school, arrive late, or miss classes altogether, affecting their concentration and academic performance.
“Financial problems affect a lot, and at times if you do not have school fees, you are chased from school,” she laments. “When you do not have transport money, you have to walk a long distance, and you might arrive late. At times, you might be tired and skip school.”
Although she has completed Senior Four, Nancy is still helping her parents at home while trying to prepare for the next stage of her education. She hopes to continue studying despite the financial obstacles threatening to delay her plans.
Poverty exposes girls to exploitation
Beyond the cost of education, Nancy says poverty can leave schoolgirls vulnerable to exploitation by wealthy men who offer money, phones, and other gifts in exchange for relationships.
She says girls struggling to meet their needs may find it difficult to reject such offers, even when they understand the risks involved.
“Wealthy men take advantage of girls and give us gifts like phones and a lot of things just because you lack money,” she said. “Such pressures can destroy a girl’s life, and she can drop out of school, get pregnant, get diseases, and lose her self-esteem. Her safety is not secure, and her future dream, like mine of becoming a pediatrician, can be destroyed easily.”
Her concerns are echoed by Dorothy Ambrose Drabuga, executive director of Women Foundation for Humanity, a women-led organization that has supported young girls, including through the provision of sanitary pads.
Drabuga says the economic crisis has made it increasingly difficult for families to provide for their children, leaving some girls vulnerable to relationships with older men who offer financial assistance.
“In the context of South Sudan, schoolgirls face a lot of challenges due to the economic hardships, and they cannot meet their needs,” she said. “This causes some of the girls to start having affairs with old men. They sleep with the girls and give them money, which is not really right.”
She says these relationships can result in early pregnancy and dropping out of school. Some pregnant girls face rejection by their families, while the men involved may deny responsibility.
Drabuga also points to economic pressures within extended families, where limited resources can affect how educational opportunities are distributed between boys and girls.
“We have extended families, and in most cases priorities are given to boys, not girls,” she said.
She argues that parents and communities should protect girls and prioritize their education instead of viewing marriage as a solution to eradicating poverty.
Drabuga says Women Foundation for Humanity and other organizations have assisted vulnerable girls with, among other things, sanitary pads and scholastic materials. However, she stresses that protecting girls and keeping them in school requires collective responsibility from parents, schools, communities and authorities.
Teachers see the effects in classrooms
The financial and social pressures girls face are reflected in classrooms, where teachers say inadequate parental support, a lack of essential supplies and household responsibilities can undermine girls’ concentration and academic performance.
Joshua Bidal Joseph, a teacher at Bulluk Secondary School who also serves as a disciplinary teacher, says some girls struggle because their families cannot afford essential school materials and menstrual hygiene products. He says the lack of such support can affect girls’ emotional well-being and ability to concentrate during lessons.
“Once a girl does not have that support to have those sanitary pads and other things, she becomes mentally tortured,” he said. “And mentally she will not focus at school.”
Bidal says teachers sometimes observe signs of distress among girls dealing with difficulties outside the classroom, including depression, reduced concentration, and challenges engaging with their studies.
“When you are teaching girls, some of them are in class, but their mind is somewhere else,” he says. “Due to things on their minds, the girls always lose focus at school.”
He adds that some girls face pressure at home, particularly those living with relatives rather than their biological parents. Household responsibilities can leave them with little time to study, while a lack of parental support may make them more vulnerable to dropping out.
The teacher says some schools try to assist struggling girls through guidance and counselling, discussions with parents and, where possible, scholarships or free education.
However, he says teachers face challenges in supporting vulnerable girls, including limited resources, insufficient time for counselling and the risk of being misunderstood when they provide individual assistance.
He urges the government to identify girls facing financial difficulties and provide sanitary pads and scholastic materials. He also calls on parents to give girls enough time to study and on teachers to continue offering guidance.
Social pressure adds to education challenges
Nancy says poverty is not the only obstacle schoolgirls face in Juba. Social media, peer pressure, parties, nightclubs, and negative friendships can also distract students from their studies.
She warns that girls may also be exposed to people who promise jobs or assistance but have harmful intentions.
“If a girl is not strong, she can lose focus on her education,” she said.
Despite these pressures, Nancy credits her family and friends for encouraging her to remain focused on her ambitions.
“My family is the biggest of all the best encouragements I have ever had. They always tell me to keep focused on my education because it is my future,” she said. “My good friends also support me, and we advise each other. When the community supports girls’ education, it gives us more courage to stay in school.”
Nancy is calling for scholarships for students who have completed Senior Four, alongside support for school materials, sanitary pads, safe transport, mentorship and counselling services in schools.
She also wants greater awareness among men and communities about the need to protect schoolgirls from exploitation and help them continue their education.
Her appeal comes as she tries to turn her childhood ambition into reality despite the financial uncertainty surrounding her next step in education.
For now, Nancy remains determined to pursue her dream of becoming a pediatrician, a profession she hopes will allow her to contribute to the well-being of children in her country.
“My dream is to become a pediatrician so I can treat and save children in South Sudan,” she said. “My message to all girls facing challenges is not to give up. I know it is hard, especially after senior four when there is no money, but your education is your future.”
“Say no to anything that will destroy your dream; stay focused, be strong, and believe that you can make it. If I, Nancy, can dream of becoming a pediatrician, you can also dream and work to realize it,” Nancy advised.

More than three years of Israel’s genocidal war has turned Gaza into “a toxic wasteland”, with poisoned water and contaminated soil threatening the survival of Palestinians in the enclave of 2.3 million people.
Israel’s use of explosives and incendiary weapons has caused environmental contamination across more than 99 percent of Gaza, according to a new report by Oxfam and the Conflict and Environment Observatory (CEOBS).

“Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza includes military assaults on its environment, which are environmental war crimes threatening life now and for generations to come,” said Amitabh Behar, Oxfam’s international executive director.
“The destruction and contamination of Gaza will have fundamentally degraded the environmental conditions necessary for human safety and survival. This would breach Israel’s legal obligations under international humanitarian and human rights law,” he said in a statement.
“Palestinians living in Gaza are being exposed to toxins in multiple ways through air, food, water and via direct contact with contaminated soils and debris.”
The report shows how Israel’s destruction of buildings and the environment has contaminated the air, soil, food and water in the enclave.
It also emphasises the urgent need for a full independent investigation to identify and reduce the risks to Palestinian lives.
Pollutants from bombardment, fires, rubble and untreated sewage can reach Palestinians through the air they breathe, the water they drink and the food they eat.
Palestinians displaced by the Israeli air and ground offensive on the Gaza Strip, walk past sewage flowing into the streets of the southern town of Khan Younis on July 4, 2024 [Jehad Alshrafi/AP Photo]   Oxfam’s report, which uses satellite imagery, remote sensing, scientific analysis and other open-source data, gives a comprehensive picture to date of the impact of the Israeli assault on Gaza, which has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians. More than 1,500 Palestinians have been killed since the so-called “ceasefire” was signed in October 2025.

items.title: AI superintelligence ‘arriving’, warns top Meta executive

original_payload.original_title: AI superintelligence ‘arriving’, warns top Meta executive
original_payload.original_body:
Meta’s top AI executive has sounded the alarm about the risk of humanity losing control of AI, warning that superintelligence that far exceeds the human intellect is imminent.
Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang issued the warning on Sunday after an employee at AI giant Anthropic announced that he had used Claude to solve the Riemann hypothesis, one of the most difficult problems in mathematics.
Recommended Stories

list 3 of 4  ‘The GOAT’: Marquez makes history with eighth MotoGP world title

Wang said the breakthrough dwarfed any human achievement for “sheer intellectual might”.
The 29-year-old executive said the milestone showed that emerging AI models will be “clearly superhuman” at improving themselves, as well as “massively accelerating” research in fields such as biology, armaments and economics.
“Superintelligence is arriving,” Wang said on X.
“How humanity acts over the next year will have great consequence on what future world we live in.”
Wang, who co-founded Scale AI before joining Meta as the tech giant’s first chief AI officer last year, said it is unlikely humankind will be able to control AI that achieves unconstrained recursive self-improvement or is “1000x smarter and more capable than humans in every field.”
“Now that we are at a point where the scientific and technical problems on capability progress are likely solved, we must not only make progress in the extremely urgent areas of safety, alignment and security, but we have to start thinking through how we progress thoughtfully,” Wang said.
AI safety advocates have identified recursive self-improvement – where AI models become capable of advancing without human input – as a critical tipping point after which humanity could lose the ability to control the technology.

Arafa Abdelaziz endured a dangerous 15-day journey from Omdurman to a displacement camp in Port Sudan in late 2023, after losing her husband and one of her two sons, who died early in the war.
Her husband died just days after fighting broke out between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in April 2023, leaving her to care for her remaining two children as their home city of Omdurman in Khartoum State came under bombardment.
Five months later, her eight-year-old son was killed by a stray bullet during clashes near Omdurman’s market.
“My son was playing outside the house with his friends when I suddenly heard a loud noise. When I went outside, I found that his head had been shattered by gunfire,” said the 33-year-old.
With the fighting between the SAF and RSF continuing in Omdurman, one of the centres of the power struggle between the two former allies at the start of the war, Arafa eventually decided to flee the city with her six-year-old son, who has a brain condition affecting his development.
Widowed women and their families live in tents with limited access to basic necessities, facing increasingly difficult living conditions. [Fatima Edam/ AlJazeera]   She describes the journey to Port Sudan as a prolonged and horrifying ordeal. Near Jebel Aulia, south of Khartoum, RSF fighters intercepted the vehicle they were in and the passengers were robbed and assaulted.

items.title: Climat : la COP31 s’achève sans accord global sur les énergies fossiles

original_payload.original_title: Climat : la COP31 s’achève sans accord global sur les énergies fossiles
original_payload.original_body:
La 31e Conférence des Nations unies sur le climat (COP31) s’est achevée dimanche 22 novembre 2026 à Antalya, en Turquie, sans accord politique global.
Après deux semaines de négociations, les représentants de près de 200 pays n’ont pas réussi à s’entendre sur un texte final, principalement en raison de leurs divergences sur la place des énergies fossiles dans la lutte contre le changement climatique.
Au cœur du blocage figure l’absence de référence explicite au charbon, au pétrole et au gaz dans le projet d’accord final, présenté par les présidences turque et australienne. Plusieurs pays, dont les membres de l’Union européenne, le Royaume-Uni, le Panama et des États insulaires, ont refusé de soutenir un texte qui ne réaffirmait pas clairement la nécessité de sortir progressivement des énergies fossiles. Ils estimaient qu’un accord climatique ne pouvait faire l’impasse sur les principales sources d’émissions de gaz à effet de serre.
À l’inverse, plusieurs pays producteurs d’hydrocarbures, notamment l’Arabie saoudite et la Russie, se sont opposés à l’introduction de références plus contraignantes aux énergies fossiles. Les discussions ont également achoppé sur la place à accorder aux technologies de captage et de stockage du carbone, ainsi que sur les engagements financiers destinés aux pays en développement.
Malgré ce blocage, des décisions distinctes ont été adoptées sur certains volets, notamment l’adaptation au changement climatique et la transition juste. Par ailleurs, près d’une centaine de pays ont soutenu un objectif visant à porter la part de l’électricité dans la consommation finale d’énergie à 35 % d’ici 2035.
Les questions non résolues devraient se poursuivre lors des prochaines négociations climatiques,  prévues en 2027 en Éthiopie.

items.title: Mayo-Kebbi Ouest : les vols de sésame inquiètent les agriculteurs du canton Kordo

original_payload.original_title: Mayo-Kebbi Ouest : les vols de sésame inquiètent les agriculteurs du canton Kordo
original_payload.original_body:
Dans le canton de Kordo, département de Nanaye, province du Mayo-Kebbi Ouest, la période de récolte du sésame est marquée par des vols répétés dans les champs. Des individus non identifiés profitent de la nuit pour emporter les récoltes déjà coupées et mises en tas, suscitant l’inquiétude des producteurs.
Alors que la récolte devrait être une période de satisfaction pour les agriculteurs, elle est devenue une source d’angoisse dans plusieurs localités du canton. Après plusieurs mois de travail, les paysans voient leurs efforts compromis par des actes de vol.
Selon plusieurs témoignages, des individus se rendent nuitamment dans les champs pour vanner le sésame déjà coupé et mis en tas, avant que les propriétaires ne puissent récupérer leur production.
Lire aussi :  Mayo-Kebbi Ouest : des habitants alertent sur la montée des tensions entre agriculteurs et éleveurs à Nanaye
En effet, après avoir coupé les tiges arrivées à maturité, les producteurs les regroupent en tas et les laissent sécher pendant environ deux semaines avant de procéder au vannage. Certains individus profiteraient de ce délai pour dérober discrètement les récoltes.
Au petit matin, les agriculteurs découvrent souvent que leurs tas ont été vannés et que le sésame a disparu. Les auteurs de ces actes, dont l’identité reste inconnue, parviennent à prendre la fuite.
Face à la répétition des vols, certains producteurs sont désormais contraints de passer des nuits entières dans leurs champs pour surveiller leurs récoltes.
Cette situation préoccupe d’autant plus les agriculteurs que le sésame constitue une importante source de revenus pour les ménages. Dans plusieurs localités du département, le kilogramme se vend actuellement entre 500 et 550 francs CFA.
Lire aussi :  Mayo-Kebbi Ouest : le préfet de Nanaye appelle les producteurs à mieux gérer leurs revenus agricoles
Pour les producteurs, protéger les récoltes revient à préserver plusieurs mois de travail et les revenus qui en dépendent.

original_payload.original_body:
Le gouvernement burkinabè annonce la fin des opérations de rapatriement de ses ressortissants installés en Guinée, à la suite des mesures d’interdiction de l’exploitation illégale de l’or prises le 2 novembre 2026. Au total, 76 169 personnes, dont 15 968 enfants, ont été rapatriées au Burkina Faso à la date du 18 novembre.
Dans un communiqué, le gouvernement burkinabè indique que ces opérations ont été organisées après des mesures ayant concerné plusieurs milliers de ses ressortissants ainsi que des citoyens d’autres pays. Après leur départ de Guinée, ces derniers ont bénéficié de l’accueil des autorités et des populations maliennes.
Face à cette situation humanitaire, le président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, a instruit le déploiement d’une mission gouvernementale à Bamako afin d’évaluer la situation et d’organiser le retour des ressortissants burkinabè dans des conditions dignes et sécurisées.
Sous la supervision du Premier ministre, le Conseil national de secours d’urgence et de réhabilitation (CONASUR) a été mobilisé pour assurer la prise en charge et le transport des personnes concernées vers leurs différentes localités d’accueil au Burkina Faso.
Selon le bilan communiqué par les autorités, les 76 169 personnes rapatriées se répartissent entre 74 452 hommes et 1 717 femmes. Parmi elles figurent 15 968 enfants.
Par ailleurs, les services d’accueil ont enregistré 1 994 ressortissants étrangers, dont deux Tchadiens. Le bilan fait également état de 983 Togolais, 580 Béninois, 150 Ivoiriens, 133 Nigériens, 53 Nigérians, 44 Maliens, 38 Ghanéens, 7 Guinéens, 3 Sierra-Léonais et 1 Sénégalais. Tous ont été pris en charge au Centre d’accueil et de transit de Bobo-Dioulasso. Des démarches sont en cours avec les ambassades de leurs pays respectifs pour organiser leur rapatriement.
Lire aussi  :  Guinée : la HAC interdit la diffusion de la télévision burkinabè RTB pour atteinte à « l’honneur, à la dignité et à l’image » de Mamadi Doumbouya
Le gouvernement précise que l’arrivée du dernier convoi, dans la nuit du 18 au 19 novembre 2026, a permis de mettre fin aux activités des sites d’accueil et d’enregistrement de Bobo-Dioulasso et de Koloko. Toutefois, les Conseils régionaux de secours d’urgence et de réhabilitation (CORESUR) restent mobilisés pour assurer le suivi des éventuels cas résiduels.
Dans son communiqué, signé par le ministre de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme, Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo, le gouvernement exprime sa reconnaissance aux autorités et au peuple maliens pour leur hospitalité et leur solidarité.
Il salue également la mobilisation du peuple burkinabè ainsi que la contribution des Forces de défense et de sécurité, des transporteurs, des organisations de la société civile, des opérateurs économiques et des personnes de bonne volonté dans la gestion de cette situation.
Enfin, les autorités burkinabè appellent l’ensemble des acteurs à accompagner les actions de réinsertion socio-économique et professionnelle des ressortissants retournés afin de faciliter leur retour à une vie stable.

Au total, 76 169 personnes, dont 15 968 enfants, ont été rapatriées au Burkina Faso à la date du 18 novembre. items.title: Perturbateurs endocriniens : une exposition possible dès la vie intra-utérine, selon l’OMS et le PNUE

original_payload.original_title: Perturbateurs endocriniens : une exposition possible dès la vie intra-utérine, selon l’OMS et le PNUE
original_payload.original_body:
Les perturbateurs endocriniens (PE), des substances chimiques susceptibles d’interférer avec le système hormonal, peuvent affecter l’organisme dès avant la naissance. C’est l’un des principaux constats du rapport conjoint de l’Organisation mondiale de la Santé (OMS) et du Programme des Nations unies pour l’Environnement (PNUE), publié en novembre 2026.
‎Intitulé « État des connaissances scientifiques sur les substances chimiques perturbatrices endocriniennes 2026 », ce document constitue la première grande actualisation mondiale depuis l’évaluation publiée par les deux institutions en 2012. Il souligne que les recherches menées au cours de la dernière décennie ont consolidé les données reliant ces substances à des effets néfastes chez l’être humain comme chez la faune sauvage.
‎Les preuves se sont renforcées concernant plusieurs domaines de santé. L’exposition aux PE est associée à des troubles de la fertilité et du développement reproductif, à des altérations du développement cérébral et des fonctions neurologiques, ainsi qu’à des perturbations de la régulation thyroïdienne et hormonale.
Lire aussi :  Moyen-Chari : des médecins sensibilisent sur la prévention du cancer du sein et des IST
‎Le rapport évoque également des liens possibles avec le métabolisme, le système immunitaire et la santé cardiovasculaire. De nouvelles préoccupations concernent les maladies métaboliques du foie et d’éventuelles atteintes rénales, même si les connaissances restent encore incomplètes dans ces domaines.
‎Ces substances ont été détectées dans le sang, le lait maternel et le sang du cordon ombilical. Une exposition survenant pendant la grossesse peut perturber l’activité hormonale et avoir des conséquences durables sur la croissance, le développement du cerveau et la santé reproductive.
Lire aussi :  Une personne sur six souffre de l’infertilité dans le monde (OMS)
‎Les PE sont présents dans de nombreux produits du quotidien, notamment les plastiques, emballages alimentaires, jouets, pesticides, produits d’hygiène et dispositifs médicaux. Parmi les composés les plus connus figurent le bisphénol A, les phtalates et les polychlorobiphényles (PCB).
‎Plus de 350 000 substances et mélanges chimiques sont utilisés dans le monde, mais seule une petite proportion a été évaluée pour déterminer si elles perturbent le système endocrinien. Le rapport rappelle également que la réglementation demeure fragmentée et que les capacités de surveillance varient fortement selon les pays.
‎Pour l’OMS et le PNUE, la prévention doit donc intervenir en amont : mieux identifier les substances à risque, renforcer la surveillance des expositions, protéger les femmes enceintes et les enfants, et encourager le remplacement des composés dangereux par des alternatives plus sûres.

items.title: ‎Cybersécurité : l’ANSICE sensibilise les étudiants de l’Université africaine de management et de l’innovation à N’Djamena

original_payload.original_title: ‎Cybersécurité : l’ANSICE sensibilise les étudiants de l’Université africaine de management et de l’innovation à N’Djamena
original_payload.original_body:
‎Le vendredi 20 novembre 2026, l’Agence nationale de sécurité informatique et de certification électronique (ANSICE) a organisé une conférence-débat à l’Université africaine de management et de l’innovation (UAMI), sur le campus de Sabangali dans le 3e arrondissement de N’Djamena.
‎
‎Placée sous le thème « De la bibliothèque classique à la bibliothèque numérique : comment télécharger et lire en toute sécurité ? », cette rencontre s’inscrivait dans le cadre de la 10ᵉ édition du Mois du livre et de la lecture. Elle avait pour objectif de sensibiliser les étudiants aux risques liés au téléchargement d’ouvrages numériques et aux précautions nécessaires pour protéger leurs données personnelles.
‎
‎Dans sa communication, Ali Barkai, directeur du contrôle et de la protection des données personnelles à l’ANSICE, a souligné que le livre numérique constitue une avancée importante dans l’accès au savoir. Il a toutefois rappelé que son utilisation exige une grande vigilance, notamment face aux risques de malwares, de phishing ou de vol de données personnelles.
‎
‎De son côté, Dr Zakit Sabit, directeur de la sécurité des systèmes d’information à l’ANSICE, a insisté sur les bonnes pratiques de cybersécurité. Il a notamment expliqué que les appareils personnels peuvent constituer des portes d’entrée vers les systèmes informatiques des institutions et des entreprises lorsqu’ils sont connectés aux réseaux professionnels.
‎
‎Il a également rappelé que les victimes d’escroqueries en ligne, de cyberharcèlement ou de cyberattaques peuvent saisir l’ANSICE, le parquet ou la Coordination de la police judiciaire, en présentant des preuves concrètes.
‎
‎« L’ANSICE est là pour protéger, sécuriser le cyberespace tchadien et traquer les cybercriminels », a-t-il assuré.

Burkina Faso : le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré inaugure l'Académie Technologique du Faso à Pabré
Le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré inaugure ce lundi l'Académie Technologique du Faso à Pabré. Une première cohorte de 250 étudiants y entame sa formation dans des secteurs stratégiques.

23 nov. 2026

Le Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, procède ce lundi 23 novembre 2026 à l’inauguration de l’Académie Technologique du Faso (ATF), située à Pabré.
Pour cette première rentrée universitaire, 250 étudiants issus des séries scientifiques et techniques ont été retenus à l’issue d’un processus de sélection. items.title: Côte d'Ivoire : Allô 101, le centre d'appels pour rapprocher les citoyens du gouvernement

original_payload.original_title: Côte d'Ivoire : Allô 101, le centre d'appels pour rapprocher les citoyens du gouvernement
original_payload.original_body:
Afrique
Côte d'Ivoire : Allô 101, le centre d'appels pour rapprocher les citoyens du gouvernement
Mis en place par le CICG, le centre d'appels gratuit Allô 101 permet aux Ivoiriens de s'informer, de signaler des situations et de lutter contre les fausses informations.
Alwihda Info
23 nov. 2026
© DR
S’informer sur les actions de l'exécutif, obtenir des réponses à ses préoccupations ou signaler une situation : les Ivoiriens disposent d’un canal dédié pour se rapprocher des pouvoirs publics. Il s’agit d’Allô 101, le centre d’appels gratuit mis en place par le Centre d’Information et de Communication Gouvernementale (CICG).
Créé en 2008, le dispositif a connu une nouvelle phase de développement avec le lancement d’une phase expérimentale en juin 2023, avant son inauguration officielle en septembre 2025.
Pour le Premier ministre, Robert Beugré Mambé, cette initiative répond à une double ambition : écouter les populations à travers le 101 et renforcer la proximité entre le gouvernement et les citoyens.
Face à la prolifération des fausses informations sur les réseaux sociaux, le ministre de la Communication et porte-parole du gouvernement, Amadou Coulibaly, insiste sur la nécessité de préserver la cohésion sociale. Il invite les populations à faire d’Allô 101 un réflexe pour s’informer.
« L’équilibre de la cohésion sociale de notre pays est menacé par les fausses informations, notamment les infox qui pullulent sur les réseaux sociaux. Je voudrais inviter nos compatriotes de toutes les catégories socioprofessionnelles à s’habituer à aller vers Allô 101 », a-t-il déclaré.
L’efficacité du dispositif repose sur sa capacité à traiter les sollicitations. Directrice du CICG, Awa Dosso souligne qu’à juillet 2025, le centre avait enregistré 1 698 055 appels. Elle met également en avant sa capacité à filtrer les appels parasites et son accessibilité sur toute l’étendue du territoire.
Accessible gratuitement sept jours sur sept, Allô 101 mobilise 60 téléopérateurs et propose une prise en charge en français, en anglais et dans 15 langues nationales. Entre juin 2023 et septembre 2026, le centre a enregistré plus de 2,1 millions d’appels.

Le Premier ministre Amadou Oury Bah a présidé, ce vendredi, l'ouverture officielle de la retraite gouvernementale. Prévue jusqu'au 24 novembre dans cette préfecture, la rencontre rassemble les membres du gouvernement, les conseillers présidentiels et les hauts fonctionnaires de l'administration.
Placée sous le thème « Renforcer la cohésion, la coordination et l'efficacité de l'action gouvernementale », cette session de travail de trois jours vise à dresser le bilan de l'exécutif et à fixer les priorités pour l'exercice 2027.
Organisée conjointement par la Primature et le Secrétariat général du gouvernement, cette enceinte fait office de cadre de concertation et d'arbitrage. Les discussions doivent déboucher sur un renforcement de la responsabilité collective, une fluidité accrue entre les ministères et une accélération des grands chantiers, au premier rang desquels figure le Programme Simandou 2040.

items.title: Cameroun : vaste opération de gendarmerie contre les coupeurs de route et les voleurs de cacao

original_payload.original_title: Cameroun : vaste opération de gendarmerie contre les coupeurs de route et les voleurs de cacao
original_payload.original_body:
Afrique
Cameroun : vaste opération de gendarmerie contre les coupeurs de route et les voleurs de cacao
Déployée le 13 novembre 2026 dans le Mbam-et-Kim, la gendarmerie a saisi armes, drogues et fèves de cacao volées lors d'une opération ciblée contre la criminalité rurale.
Alwihda Info
23 nov. 2026
© DR
Dans le cadre de l'opération « Tentacules », la gendarmerie a mené une vaste descente dans le département du Mbam-et-Kim pour neutraliser plusieurs sanctuaires criminogènes. Cette intervention, débutée le 13 novembre 2026, vise à enrayer la recrudescence des braquages et des vols de cacao qui touchent les planteurs en pleine campagne.
Au total, 46 militaires — dont 30 issus de la Légion de Gendarmerie du Centre et 16 de l'état-major de la compagnie de Ntui — ont été mobilisés sous la supervision du commandant de compagnie. Les patrouilles et les fouilles systématiques se concentrent sur les localités de Banta, Ngoke 1 et 2, Longue, ainsi que sur l'épicentre de Voundou et les villages de Yangafock 1 et 2.
Les premiers ratissages sur les axes de transit du cacao ont permis la saisie de plusieurs types de stupéfiants et substances psychotropes, incluant du cannabis, du Tramadol et d'autres produits pharmaceutiques illicites. Les forces de l'ordre ont également mis la main sur des sacs de fèves de cacao humides, du matériel présumé volé au préjudice des agriculteurs, ainsi que des outils d'effraction tels que des pinces Monseigneur, des machettes et des pieds de biche.
Côté armement, deux pistolets automatiques et plusieurs fusils de calibre 12 ont été récupérés. Les suspects interpellés au cours de cette opération sont actuellement entendus par les enquêteurs. L'intervention se poursuit sur le terrain dans l'attente d'un bilan définitif.

items.title: Why is Bangladesh’s Grameen Bank under attack?

original_payload.original_title: Why is Bangladesh’s Grameen Bank under attack?
original_payload.original_body:
Dhaka, Bangladesh –  When attackers stormed a Grameen Bank branch in Kashiani last week, they did not just damage furniture and equipment. They also destroyed records accumulated over nearly three decades.
Solaiman Morol, the branch manager in Bangladesh’s Gopalganj district, said about a dozen men arrived on the afternoon of November 18 carrying machetes, petrol and tools to break the locks. Staff members were away on field visits.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items    list 1 of 4  Home of Bangladesh’s former leader Muhammad Yunus set on fire
list 2 of 4  Myanmar, China object to landmark ICJ ruling on Rohingya genocide
list 3 of 4  ‘Disappointing’: Delegates react after COP31 climate talks end without deal
list 4 of 4  Spontaneous or orchestrated? Violent pro-Hasina protests rock Bangladesh
end of list
The attackers looted the branch and tried to cut open its vault with a grinder. They took out about 40 sacks of vouchers and other documents and set them on fire. They also looted steel cupboards, filing cabinets, chairs, tables and other equipment. A staff member’s rice cooker was among the items taken away. “They said that after burning the records, nobody would have to repay their loans,” Morol said.
Videos of the attack later appeared online. Morol said he heard slogans including “Joy Bangla” and “Joy Bangabandhu”, associated with  ousted former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina ’s Awami League, as well as calls to burn what the attackers described as “Yunus’s den”.
The branch has not been able to resume normal operations. Staff members have received threats and customers are worried about the safety of their deposits and loan records.
“A bank depends on trust. This is impacting our customers’ confidence. People who have deposits with us are becoming frightened,” Morol said.
It wasn’t a one-off incident.
Grameen Bank under attack
The attack was part of a wider wave of violence against Grameen Bank. Its latest internal memorandum, dated November 23, records 97 attacks on branches and offices between November 10 and 23.

items.title: Occupied West Bank ‘military zones’ become de facto Israeli settler land

original_payload.original_title: Occupied West Bank ‘military zones’ become de facto Israeli settler land
original_payload.original_body:
Ramallah, Occupied West Bank –  Saleh Zahran had a room on his family’s land with a television, a fireplace, a fridge and solar panels. The kids would play in the groves, and the men stayed up late at night watching the stars.
“We’d cook, eat, drink, spend a whole day from morning to sunset,” he says.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items    list 1 of 3  Israeli settlers attack several Palestinian villages in occupied West Bank
list 2 of 3  Is the global far right really in retreat?
list 3 of 3  Israeli attacks on medics in occupied West Bank surge by 350%: Rights group
end of list
Zahran, 39, inherited the farmland, with 120 olive trees, in Deir Abu Mishal, a village west of Ramallah, from his grandfather and father, splitting it among his brothers.
Between 70 and 80 percent of people in the village, which falls in Area B, under joint Israeli-Palestinian control, live off the land, and just a few years ago, there were no settlers nearby.
“We’d come and go whenever we wanted, pick our fruit at our own pace, sell, build, and marry off sons from the olives. Now, it’s all gone,” he told Al Jazeera.
Since settlers set up an outpost in Area B about 1km from his land in June, nobody in his family had been able to reach it. Settlers attacked their cars, and his elderly father was pepper-sprayed while trying to reach the farmland, he says.
On November 10, an Israeli High Court decision granted the village two days of army “coordinated” harvesting, something once unthinkable in Area B.
Zahran set out with his brothers to reach their lands for the first time in five months, but about 20 settlers came at them. They threw stones, smashed the family’s truck and his brother’s four-wheeler and slashed the tyres. He saw no soldiers, and police never arrived despite their calls.
The next day, the army and its liaison office were present. But farmers were held up until about 9am, shown a map of permitted areas, and told to leave by 2:30pm. Ghiyath Nasser, their lawyer, says villagers could reach less than a third of the area in question, so Zahran could harvest only about 20 of his 120 trees.
Old aerial photo of Saleh Zahran’s property in Deir Abu Mishal [Al Jazeera]   After five months, Zahran finally reached the farm room that day only to find settlers had stolen or smashed his belongings and were drawing water for their sheep from the two wells he had restored. The saplings he had planted last year had died of thirst.

The COP31 climate summit in Turkey ended in deadlock on Sunday, with countries failing to reach agreement on key issues including fossil fuels, climate finance and carbon-removal technologies, raising fresh questions about the future of global climate negotiations.

The FG maintained that despite the lack of a finalised deal, Nigeria would not stop its domestic climate programmes.
In a statement released on Sunday after the fallout, the Director-General, National Council on Climate Change, Omotenioye Majekodunmi, said Nigeria would continue implementing its climate commitments under its Nationally Determined Contribution 3.0, strengthening climate governance and attracting investment into the energy transition.
She said, “COP31’s inability to reach consensus on an overarching political outcome is disappointing and underscores the continuing challenges facing international climate cooperation. items.title: PUBLIC NOTICE: ALL STAKEHOLDERS, (POLICYHOLDERS; FORMER STAFF; SHAREHOLDERS AND CREDITORS OF NIGER INSURANCE PLC (UNDER RECEIVERSHIP)

original_payload.original_title: PUBLIC NOTICE: ALL STAKEHOLDERS, (POLICYHOLDERS; FORMER STAFF; SHAREHOLDERS AND CREDITORS OF NIGER INSURANCE PLC (UNDER RECEIVERSHIP)
original_payload.original_body:
UPDATE ON STATE OF AFFAIRS/STATEMENT OF FACTS OF THE COMPANY AND DEVELOPMENTS RELATED THERETO — BY THE RECEIVER AND LIQUIDATOR
It will be recalled that the undersigned did a publication on July 17, 2026, briefing all stakeholders of Niger Insurance, Plc. on state of affairs of the company, following a judgment of 5 th  June, 2026 in  Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/887/2025,  obtained in the name of the Company, without authority, by individuals who have no stake or shareholding in the company, but claiming to be Board Members of the company under Receivership/Liquidation.
For the purpose of those who must have missed the said publication, we shall restate in brief some salient facts contained therein, and thereafter state developments in respect of the company,  vis-à-vis,  position of the cases in the Appellate Courts, as at date:
The operating license of Niger Insurance Plc. was cancelled by the official Regulatory Agency (National Insurance Commission) ,  otherwise known as NAICOM, in  June, 2022  for gross infraction against the prevailing Insurance Act and also for inability of the company to fulfill her core statutory obligations, i.e., payment of verified claims of its policy holders, since 2013 and inability to pay its staff salaries for well over a period of time, preceding 30 calendar months; after the company admitted those infractions in writing.
In reaction to the license cancellation, the company immediately afterwards instituted an action at the Federal High Court Abuja, challenging the license cancellation and appointment of a Receiver/Liquidator for the company, by the Commission.
The Federal High Court, Abuja, struck out the Suit for being incompetent and for lack of jurisdiction. The company immediately challenged that decision in an appeal to the Court of Appeal.
The said Appeal was eventually dismissed by the Court of Appeal in  2024 , following the filing of Notice of Withdrawal of the Appeal by the company.
The company subsequently made a volve face and, engaged the services of another counsel (also a SAN) to file an application at the Court of Appeal to relist the dismissed Appeal, but the application was unanimously rejected and dismissed by the Court of Appeal sitting in Abuja, on the  27th of February, 2025.
Dissatisfied with the decision of the Court of Appeal refusing to relist the dismissed appeal, the company went on further appeal to the Supreme Court; all the briefs of Argument have been duly filed and exchanged by the parties, but no hearing date has yet being given by the Apex Court.
It was while the appeal on the subject matter of cancellation of the company license and appointment of a Receiver/Liquidator by the Commission was pending at the Supreme Court that the individuals who claimed to be Board members of the company in Receiver/Liquidation, initiated an action before the same Federal High Court, presided over, this time, by Hon. Justice J.K. Omotosho, vide an Amended Originating Summons dated 30th April, 2025 but filed on the 11th July, 2025; which action birthed the referenced judgment of 5 th  June, 2026 despite bringing to the attention of that Court the glaring issue of abuse of Court process involved.
As mentioned above, despite the fact that attention of Justice Omotosho, via a Notice of Preliminary Objection, was pointedly drawn to the facts that the principal claims, issues and subject matters of the fresh case before him had been ruled upon by his fellow Judge of the same status ( Coram: Ekwo, J.) in January,  2023, and that the matter is now on appeal at the Supreme Court, awaiting determination on whether the Court of Appeal was right to dismiss the appeal of the company over the decision of Ekwo, J.,  the learned Justice Omotosho proceeded to hear the matter expeditiously, and gave judgment to the Plaintiffs on 5 th  June 2026 .
The National Insurance Commission and the Receiver promptly filed their Notices of appeal against the judgement, of Omotosho, J. raising grounds of abuse of court process and also lack of jurisdiction/competence of the Presiding Judge, the fresh action having been barred by Statute of Limitation, having not been filed within the mandatory 3 months of occurrence of the alleged injurious actions of NAICOM, and their having to wait for over 2 calendar years after the said acts, before instituting the said fresh case in 2026, brought before Justice Omotosho.
It should also be noted that both the Commission, (NAICOM) and the Receiver also filed along with their respective Notices of Appeal, Motions for Stay of Execution, by their Counsel, i.e., office of  Prof Osipitan, SAN & Co, and Tochukwu, SAN & CO,  at the Court of Appeal and the appeal, inclusive of the applications, are pending.
It is also pertinent to note that the briefs of Argument had been filed by the parties Counsel, inclusive of Reply brief, and all being awaited now is hearing date from the Appeal Court Registry. Same goes with the earlier Appeal at the Apex Court in respect of the Court of Appeal dismissal of the challenge to the 2023 Ekwo, J’s judgment. The above stated scenario represents the undisputable development in the 3 cases cited above, all relating to Niger Insurance Plc,  vis, a vis,  efforts that had been made to circumvent due process of law, abuse of judicial process and the rule of law, by some known characters in this matter.
It is pertinent to state that following the cancellation of the company’s operating license in June 2022 by the Commission/NAICOM and appointment of the Receiver, no shareholder of the company had opposed the actions taken by the Commission till date, albeit, gone to Court to challenge same, neither has any duly constituted Board of the company met to take any decision concerning the subject matter, or the company in general.
The instituting of the case challenging the action of the Commission in June, 2022, was actually instigated and carried out on the instruction of a minority shareholder, without consultation with any of the company’s other shareholders.
The shareholder in question is merely one of the shareholders of the Plc company, and has only  about 25%  of Niger Insurance, Plc Shareholding, going by  the last approved audited statement of the Company, and certainly not its majority shareholder.  The authenticity of this fact can also be confirmed from the Commission, by any stakeholder.

original_payload.original_title: Soja au Bénin : pas de prix plancher, 450 000 tonnes de capacités industrielles
original_payload.original_body:

Soja au Bénin : pas de prix plancher, 450 000 tonnes de capacités industrielles
Le gouvernement confirme la liberté des prix du soja pour 2026-2027. Il surveille les négociations, tandis que les industriels doivent s’approvisionner localement.
Personnalités dans cet article

Ajouter Bénin Web TV à vos sources préférées
SOMMAIRE
Une prime de 10 FCFA soumise à une condition
Au Bénin, le gouvernement maintient l’absence de prix plancher et de prix plafond pour la commercialisation du soja au cours de la campagne 2026-2027. Le porte-parole de l’exécutif, Wilfried Léandre Houngbédji, l’a confirmé dimanche 22 novembre sur Bénin TV, en défendant la négociation directe des tarifs entre producteurs et acheteurs.
Le ministre a évoqué une production nationale d’environ 800 000 tonnes de soja et des besoins de l’ordre de 450 000 tonnes pour les unités industrielles installées dans le pays. Ces volumes placent l’approvisionnement des transformateurs au centre des discussions commerciales, alors que les agriculteurs réclament des conditions de vente rémunératrices.
La campagne a démarré le 6 novembre sur le marché intérieur, selon les modalités fixées par le communiqué interministériel du 4 novembre. Les ventes se font au prix convenu entre les parties. Les exportations de fèves, elles, ne pourront commencer que le 15 février 2027, un calendrier destiné à laisser aux usines locales la possibilité de se fournir en priorité.
La liberté des prix avait déjà été retenue pour la campagne précédente. Face aux inquiétudes sur le poids des acheteurs dans la négociation, Wilfried Léandre Houngbédji a assuré que l’État continuait de suivre le marché. Les organisations interprofessionnelles peuvent notamment porter à la connaissance des autorités les difficultés et pratiques abusives signalées par leurs membres.
Une prime de 10 FCFA soumise à une condition
Le prix libre ne supprime pas les mesures de soutien annoncées aux producteurs. Le  Conseil des ministres du 3 juin 2026  a institué, pour le soja, une prime exceptionnelle de 10 FCFA par kilogramme livré aux unités de transformation locales, une fois leurs capacités installées satisfaites. Le volume de référence retenu pour la campagne 2026-2027 est de 450 000 tonnes.
Ce dispositif est distinct du prix de vente, qui demeure déterminé par la négociation commerciale. Le même mécanisme de prime a été annoncé pour l’anacarde et le riz, avec des capacités de transformation retenues respectivement à 200 000 et 350 000 tonnes.
Le ministère du Commerce intérieur a parallèlement rappelé, le 11 novembre, que l’approvisionnement en soja devait rester libre et que les documents présentés comme des « droits d’approvisionnement » n’étaient pas autorisés. Lors de son intervention du 22 novembre, le porte-parole du gouvernement a invité les acteurs de la filière à faire remonter les éventuelles dérives aux autorités compétentes.

Matty Cash devrait manquer le déplacement d’Aston Villa chez Galatasaray, mardi 24 novembre à 18 h 45, heure de Cotonou, pour la cinquième journée de la Ligue des champions. Victime d’une commotion cérébrale avec la Pologne le 14 novembre, le latéral droit est toujours soumis à un protocole de reprise. Selon  BirminghamLive , une période de douze jours sans compétition doit également l’écarter du rendez-vous européen.
Le défenseur de 29 ans a reçu un coup au visage lors de la défaite de la Pologne en Roumanie (1-2), avant de sortir à la 76e minute. Vendredi 20 novembre, Unai Emery a confirmé son forfait contre Sunderland, rencontré le lendemain et tenu en échec par Villa (0-0). Le  communiqué médical du club  mentionne le protocole pour les commotions cérébrales. Aston Villa n’a pas encore officialisé son absence pour mardi.
Unai Emery dispose néanmoins d’une solution au poste de latéral droit. L’international congolais  Aaron Wan-Bissaka, remis d’une blessure après six matchs manqués , a retrouvé la compétition contre Sunderland. Johan Manzambi s’est lui aussi remis d’une douleur au mollet et a repris les entraînements collectifs. Matteo Ruggeri et Amadou Onana restent indisponibles.
Aston Villa compte neuf points après quatre rencontres européennes. Les Anglais ont battu le Club Bruges, Fenerbahçe et Viking avant de s’incliner à Barcelone. Galatasaray en totalise six, obtenus contre Lille et Stuttgart, et cherche à se rapprocher des places qualificatives avant de recevoir son adversaire anglais au RAMS Park.

Le bilan de l’accident de la route survenu samedi 21 novembre 2026 à Guéné, dans la commune de Malanville, est passé à six morts. Une personne grièvement blessée lors de la collision entre un bus de transport en commun et un tricycle a succombé après son évacuation à l’hôpital.
Le drame s’est produit aux environs de 9 heures. Le bus appartient à une compagnie nigérienne de transport de voyageurs. Le tricycle transportait plusieurs passagers au moment du choc, dans cette localité du département de l’Alibori.
Le premier bilan faisait état de cinq personnes décédées et de plusieurs blessés. L’un d’eux avait été conduit en urgence dans un établissement de santé. Son décès a été rapporté par la radio Sota FM, puis relayé lundi 23 novembre par Banouto.
Une équipe de la Police républicaine s’est rendue sur les lieux pour procéder aux constatations après la collision, rapportait Le Matinal dimanche 22 novembre.
Guéné avait déjà connu un accident meurtrier le 22 septembre 2025. Dans le village de Goungoun, au sein du même arrondissement, une autre collision avait provoqué  la mort de quatre personnes et fait plusieurs blessés .

Carlos Alcaraz a remporté son premier titre aux ATP Finals, dimanche 22 novembre à Turin. L’Espagnol a dominé le numéro un mondial Alexander Zverev en deux sets, 6-2, 7-6(7), au terme d’une finale maîtrisée en un peu plus de deux heures.
Alcaraz a rapidement pris l’ascendant dans la première manche. Plus incisif en retour, il est devenu le premier joueur du tournoi à prendre le service de Zverev et a conclu le set 6-2, malgré un débreak concédé en cours de route.
Le deuxième set a été plus disputé. Zverev a poussé son adversaire jusqu’au jeu décisif et s’est procuré trois balles de set consécutives. Alcaraz les a toutes écartées avant de s’imposer 9-7 dans le tie-break.
À 23 ans, le Murcien devient le troisième Espagnol à gagner le Masters de fin de saison. Finaliste battu par Jannik Sinner en 2025, il ajoute à son palmarès le principal trophée du circuit qui lui échappait encore en dehors des tournois du Grand Chelem.
Ce succès constitue son sixième titre de la saison et le 30e de sa carrière. Il prolonge également une série de 14 victoires consécutives et signe un troisième sacre d’affilée, après ceux de Vienne et du Masters 1000 de Paris.
La fin d’année tranche avec le printemps du joueur espagnol, éloigné des courts pendant quatre mois en raison d’une blessure au poignet. Depuis son élimination en quarts de finale de l’US Open, il affiche 22 victoires pour une seule défaite.
Zverev termine néanmoins la saison à la première place mondiale après avoir remporté ses deux premiers titres du Grand Chelem en 2026. Alcaraz porte désormais son bilan face à l’Allemand à huit victoires contre six, avec un premier succès obtenu en salle.

Emmanuel Emegha a vécu une journée contrastée pour sa première titularisation avec Chelsea. Auteur de son premier but sous le maillot londonien face à Leeds, l’attaquant néerlandais a annoncé dimanche sur Instagram avoir été victime d’un vol après la rencontre.
« Malheureusement, après le match, j’ai été victime d’un vol. Je vais bien et, heureusement, personne n’a été blessé », a écrit le joueur de 23 ans. Il a également remercié les personnes qui lui ont adressé des messages de soutien.
Cette annonce est intervenue au terme d’un match où Emegha avait rapidement trouvé l’ouverture. Servi par Morgan Rogers, il a marqué à la 25e minute d’une frappe du pied gauche au premier poteau, donnant l’avantage à Chelsea à Stamford Bridge.
Leeds a toutefois égalisé moins de trois minutes plus tard par Noah Okafor. Dominic Calvert-Lewin a ensuite transformé un penalty au retour des vestiaires, avant un second but d’Okafor et une dernière réalisation de Brenden Aaronson dans le temps additionnel. Les visiteurs se sont imposés 4-1.
Emegha a disputé 64 minutes avant de céder sa place à Danny Welbeck. Cette rencontre constituait sa première titularisation complète et son premier but avec Chelsea, après une entrée progressive dans l’effectif londonien cette saison.
Dans son message, le joueur a aussi annoncé vouloir revenir plus fort vendredi. Chelsea se déplacera à Nottingham Forest le 27 novembre, avec un coup d’envoi prévu à 20 heures.

Hakan Çalhanoğlu a quitté prématurément la pelouse, dimanche 22 novembre, lors du match nul de l’Inter Milan sur le terrain de l’Atalanta (4-4). Le milieu turc a été remplacé par Petar Sučić à la 33e minute, peu après le deuxième but de Francesco Pio Esposito. items.title: COP31 : le pacte d’Antalya échoue sur les énergies fossiles et les financements

original_payload.original_title: COP31 : le pacte d’Antalya échoue sur les énergies fossiles et les financements
original_payload.original_body:
Accueil

COP31 : le pacte d’Antalya échoue sur les énergies fossiles et les financements
Le sommet climatique s’est achevé dimanche 22 novembre sans décision politique générale. L’adaptation et la transition juste ont néanmoins fait l’objet d’accords.
Environnement      Par  Diane Mireille Niyonzima
·   23 Nov. 2026 à 08:53  23/11/26 08:53       ·   2 min  de lecture
Lire hors-ligne
Écouter
Sauvegarder           Commentaires  (0)   0              Partager
Murat Kurum et Wopke Hoekstra lors de la pré-COP31 à Nadi, aux Fidji (archives). Photo : Union européenne, 2026 / Zafiya Shamim, FACTSTORY, CC BY 4.0 (format adapté).
Partager
Ajouter Bénin Web TV à vos sources préférées
La COP31 s’est achevée dimanche 22 novembre 2026 à Antalya, en Turquie, sans adoption du « pacte d’Antalya », la décision politique centrale attendue à l’issue du sommet des Nations unies sur le climat. Après près de cinquante heures de prolongation des négociations, le président de la conférence, Murat Kurum, a constaté l’absence de consensus entre les délégations.
Le projet préparé sous les présidences turque et australienne ne mentionnait pas explicitement la transition hors des énergies fossiles, pourtant actée lors de la COP28 en 2023. L’Union européenne, le Royaume-Uni, la Norvège et plusieurs États insulaires ont refusé de l’approuver. Le recours à la capture du carbone, présenté dans le projet, a aussi suscité des objections parmi les pays exposés aux conséquences du réchauffement.
Les discussions sur le financement ont révélé d’autres divergences. Le Groupe africain a critiqué la proposition de tripler les financements destinés à l’adaptation sans préciser clairement la base de calcul. Il a également soulevé des réserves sur les garanties d’application de la feuille de route Antalya-Addis-Abeba. Malgré ces objections, les représentants africains se disaient disposés à accepter le texte comme compromis, tandis que d’autres délégations ont maintenu leur opposition.
L’échec du pacte principal n’a pas empêché l’adoption de décisions sur l’objectif mondial d’adaptation, le Fonds pour l’adaptation et le programme de travail pour une transition juste. Les discussions ont en revanche échoué sur plusieurs autres projets, notamment ceux concernant l’atténuation des émissions et le Fonds pour l’environnement mondial. L’initiative d’ électrification mondiale à l’horizon 2035 , défendue par la Turquie à l’ouverture du sommet, n’a pas permis de débloquer le compromis politique général.
Dans son  intervention officielle de clôture , le secrétaire exécutif de la Convention des Nations unies sur les changements climatiques, Simon Stiell, a reconnu l’échec des décisions portées par les présidences tout en rappelant les accords obtenus dans les autres négociations. Les engagements climatiques adoptés lors des conférences précédentes demeurent applicables.
La prochaine conférence annuelle, la COP32, doit se tenir en Éthiopie du 8 au 19 novembre 2027. Elle sera notamment attendue sur les engagements financiers et la poursuite des discussions relatives aux combustibles fossiles.

original_payload.original_title: Nigeria : la sanction à vie de Chioma Ajunwa ramenée au temps déjà purgé
original_payload.original_body:
Accueil
